_comment: Positions ledger for report.py. The trading session maintains it: a buy APPENDS, a sell REMOVES. sleeve = swing|momentum (NO 'legacy' — every position is judged each run with a take-profit / trail / hold / thesis-check action; treat the book as an income / grow-the-balance portfolio). Stops are TRAILING: a winner carries a GTC stop ~15% below its running high, ratcheted UP only and never below entry, so it can only ever be sold for a locked-in gain; underwater names carry NO price stop and are thesis-managed (sell only if the thesis breaks, else cull at the monthly rebalance). Options positions (sleeve:'options') may carry a 'manual_hold_override' field to suspend ONLY the mechanical -50% price stop (see CLAUDE.md HARD RULE 8) — settable/clearable only by a genuinely interactive session with a real, live Ryan turn, never by an automated run (same bar as HARD RULE 9).

_LEGGING_TESTED_AND_BLOCKED.the_mechanism: A spread's risk offset exists ONLY INSIDE a multi-leg order. Sent alone, leg two is not 'the short leg of a spread' -- the broker cannot know a long 695P is meant to cover it -- so it is margined STANDALONE as a cash-secured put and demands the entire strike in collateral. Legging destroys the exact property that makes a vertical capital-efficient. A legged CALL spread is worse: a standalone short call is NAKED (cash.infinite=true), banned outright at any level.
_LEGGING_TESTED_AND_BLOCKED.why_this_upgrades_the_prior_warning: CLAUDE.md already warned that a rejected leg two would leave an orphaned full-premium single leg. That was rated a RISK. This measurement makes it a CERTAINTY: leg one fills, leg two is rejected for collateral, and the sleeve owns a position it never decided to own at 4-9x the vertical's theta. Long-first ordering prevents a naked short; it does NOT prevent the orphan.
_LEGGING_TESTED_AND_BLOCKED.review_is_trustworthy_HERE_do_not_overge: The multi-leg FALSE GREEN happens because multi-leg SUPPORT is validated only at the place endpoint. This is a COLLATERAL/buying-power check, which review does perform and did surface correctly. So a clean review still proves nothing about multi-leg support, but a review raising a collateral alert is real and must be honoured.
_LEGGING_TESTED_AND_BLOCKED.the_workflow_that_DOES_preserve_spread_e: Do not leg it, and do not quietly substitute a single leg and call it the same trade. When a thesis genuinely wants a vertical: fully spec it -- both legs, net debit, max profit, breakevens, invalidation -- and hand it to Ryan to place in the Robinhood app, where multi-leg works normally. Desk does the analysis, Ryan does the execution. The permanent fix is agentic multi-leg support.
_LEGGING_TESTED_AND_BLOCKED.nothing_was_placed: This was review_option_order only, which does not place. No order was sent, no position opened, and no naked short was ever created or contemplated -- the review was run precisely to avoid discovering this mid-leg with a live long already on the books.

_MULTICONTRACT_SIZING_FINDING.headline: A CHEAP UNDERLYING IS NOT AN UNAFFORDABLE ONE. Multi-contract sizing fills the size bands on low-priced liquid ETFs without degrading a single ratio any gate measures -- and the desk has never used it.
_MULTICONTRACT_SIZING_FINDING.the_false_constraint_caught_before_it_wa: TLT's 84C costs $59.50. XLP, XLF, XLU and XLE trade at $43-86 spot. The natural inference -- and the one this run was on the point of recording as a structural exclusion -- is that these names cannot produce a $300-1,000 TACTICAL or $500-1,000 CORE position and are therefore out of reach, a tidy mirror of the documented 'AMD is priced out' tier finding.
_MULTICONTRACT_SIZING_FINDING.why_it_is_wrong_measured_not_modelled: Spread as a percentage of mid is a PER-CONTRACT property, entirely independent of quantity. TEN TLT 2026-09-18 84C = $595.00, dead centre of the CORE band, at 1.68% of mid, delta 0.415, OI 51,155, with a 546 x 784 book that absorbs the size without strain. Every ratio the gates actually test -- spread %, delta, OI, DTE, premium at risk -- is identical or better than a single-contract position on a pricier name.
_MULTICONTRACT_SIZING_FINDING.what_it_opens: The liquid low-priced ETF universe (TLT, XLP, XLF, XLU, XLE and peers) is available to BOTH tracks and has never been hunted. It matters most on exactly the days that keep stalling this desk: when index and mega-cap boards are blocked by one single-name earnings print, these instruments are uncorrelated with it and quote far tighter than the equity report's mid-cap screen -- 1.68% of mid today against that screen's 12.6-52%.
_MULTICONTRACT_SIZING_FINDING.the_honest_limits: Three, so no future run over-reads this. (1) It supplies NO thesis -- this run measured the chain and still declined the trade. (2) Per-contract commissions scale with quantity where they apply, so a 10-lot pays ten times any per-contract fee even though the spread ratio is unchanged; check the fee line in review_option_order before sizing large lots. (3) Depth must be verified at the intended size, not assumed from OI -- 51,155 OI with a 546 x 784 top-of-book is fine for a 10-lot and would not be for a 500-lot.
_MULTICONTRACT_SIZING_FINDING.the_transferable_lesson: This is the FOURTH instance of this file's oldest bug and the FIRST caught before being written down rather than after. Spot price (2026-08-14), ATM strike (2026-08-17), wrong expiry board (2026-08-24), and now quantity-of-one. Each time a name was declared untradeable from a quote that was never the test. The fix never changes: QUOTE IT. And note the asymmetry that makes this one worth keeping -- the previous three instances wrongly EXCLUDED tradeable names, and so did this one; the bug has never once erred toward taking a bad trade, which is precisely why it survives so long unnoticed.

_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.subject: THE CONCURRENT-RUN COLLISION FINALLY HAPPENED ON THE EQUITY BOOK, AND IT BREACHED THE CASH FLOOR BY AN AMOUNT NEITHER RUN COULD HAVE SEEN. The mitigation CLAUDE.md prescribes -- re-fetch origin/master before placing -- WAS PERFORMED, CORRECTLY, AND DID NOT WORK. Measured 2026-08-28T13:50Z.
_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.what_happened: Two scheduler-fired runs executed the same first-post-open slot: session ...OfEc (fired 13:30:28Z) and session ...1TG2 (fired 13:38Z). Each read the same committed report, each ran the full v8 gate stack, each graded the screen independently, and each took its own 1-of-1 per-run equity entry. ...OfEc bought ROST 2 sh @ 230.1512 = $460.30, filled 13:37:13Z. ...1TG2 bought MDLZ 7.988509 sh @ 62.59 = $500.00, filled ~13:40Z. Both entries are individually sound and both survive review on their merits -- this is NOT a case of a bad trade.
_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.the_arithmetic_that_matters: EACH RUN'S SIZING WAS COMPLIANT ALONE; THE PAIR IS NOT. Pre-trade the equity book was cash $2,507.26 / equity $939.45, so the posture's max compliant buy was 2507.26 - 0.45 x 3446.71 = $956.24 -- and $460.30 and $500.00 each sit comfortably under it. Together they are $960.30, which is $4.06 OVER. Measured live at 13:47Z: cash $1,546.96, equity_value $1,892.33, book $3,439.29, floor reading 44.98% against the >=45% Aug-Oct minimum. On cost rather than marks it is 44.88%. The breach is real and it is small -- roughly $4 of a $3,440 book, 0.12pp.
_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.why_the_prescribed_mitigation_failed_and: CLAUDE.md says: 'BEFORE any place order, re-fetch origin/master and re-read holdings.json + trade_journal.json. If a sibling entry has landed since this run began, DEFER.' ...OfEc performed exactly that at 13:36:59Z and master was clean at cda3f4e. It WAS clean -- the sibling had not yet committed. THE LEDGER LAGS A SIBLING'S FILL BY THAT SIBLING'S COMMIT LATENCY, which here was about 2.5 minutes (ROST filled 13:37:13Z, the commit recording it landed ~13:47Z). A git-based check therefore has a blind window exactly as long as the other run's write-up, and a run that researches carefully before committing is a run whose fill is invisible for LONGER. The check is not merely imperfect; it is systematically blind in the direction that matters.
_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.THE_FIX: RE-READ THE BROKER, NOT ONLY origin/master, IMMEDIATELY BEFORE ANY ORDER: get_equity_positions and get_portfolio for equities, get_option_positions for options. The broker reflects a sibling's fill in the same second; the repository reflects it minutes later. Then recompute the gate off THOSE numbers rather than off the numbers read at run start. PROVEN ON THIS EXACT INCIDENT: had ...1TG2 re-read the broker at ~13:39Z it would have seen ROST already held, giving cash $2,046.96 / equity ~$1,399.75 and a max compliant buy of 2046.96 - 0.45 x 3446.71 = $495.94. Its $500.00 order was $4.06 over that -- so a broker re-read would have caught this breach precisely, and a $495 order would have been fully compliant. The fix is not theoretical; it closes THIS hole exactly.
_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.second_order_lesson: A pre-trade gate computed at RUN START is stale by the time the order is sent, even with no sibling involved -- marks move. The cash floor in particular is defined as a function of live cash and live equity value, so it must be recomputed from a fresh get_portfolio at order time. 'I checked the floor this run' is not the same claim as 'the floor holds at the moment I am sending this order'.
_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.what_was_NOT_done_and_why: NEITHER POSITION WAS UNWOUND TO CURE THE BREACH. Restoring 45% requires raising about $4 of cash; selling a $4 sliver of a position pays a spread and a round trip to correct a rounding-scale overshoot, and the floor is written as a SIZING gate ('compute it BEFORE proposing a size', 'max compliant buy = ...'), not as a continuous constraint that forces liquidation -- ordinary mark drift moves this reading across 45% daily in either direction. The correct response is to STOP ADDING, which is what has been done: the equity book is closed to further entries today until the floor reads >=45% again. Reported to Ryan the same session rather than buried in a ledger key.
_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.MDLZ_LEDGER_OWNERSHIP: RESOLVED at the final merge: the sibling committed MDLZ to positions[] in PR #790 (7.988509 sh @ 62.5899, order 6a918fb3), so the ledger now carries all four equity positions and matches the broker one-for-one. The earlier concern -- that writing the position from this side would duplicate it -- was correct and the deliberate omission was the right call; the sibling's own record landed intact.
_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.cross_reference: Precedent: the 2026-08-13 collision (13:00Z/13:10Z and 17:02Z/17:05Z pairs) which cost nothing because both runs declined. CLAUDE.md predicted this exact escalation -- 'two concurrent runs finding the same A-grade setup would BOTH place it' -- and the only thing it got wrong is that they found DIFFERENT setups, so the breach came through the shared cash floor rather than through a doubled position.
_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.only_ryan_can_fix_the_root: The redundant trigger configuration (cron-job.org sub-hourly + the routine's native hourly backstop) is what puts two runs in one slot, and it is Ryan's to change. _CROSS_BOOK_CASH_COUPLING.status: DURABLE capital-rule finding. Not session-scoped; do not delete at the bell.
_CROSS_BOOK_CASH_COUPLING.claim: The options sleeve and the equity book are separable in their CAPS and NOT in their CASH. Premium spent by the options sleeve leaves the same `cash` field that is the NUMERATOR of the >=45% equity-book cash floor, so every options entry deepens the floor breach and pushes the equity book's reopening further away.
_CROSS_BOOK_CASH_COUPLING.why_the_pinned_rule_misses_it: CLAUDE.md pins the floor as cash / (cash + equity_value), EXCLUDING options_value, because the sleeve 'must not be double-counted against the equity cash floor.' That pin governs the DENOMINATOR and is correct. It is silent on the NUMERATOR, where the sleeve's cash draw is counted unavoidably. The rule is right and answers a different question than the one that bites -- which is why several sessions of runs have quoted it without noticing.

quantified_at_2026-08-28_capital.marginal_rates: 1.60 floor-points per $100 of OPTIONS premium; 2.91 per $100 of EQUITY purchase. Equity costs ~1.8x more per dollar -- but the options number is NOT ZERO, and the 'separate book' framing invites treating it as zero.
quantified_at_2026-08-28_capital.worked_consequence: A single $500 TACTICAL scalp -- entirely ordinary inside THE FOUR LAWS' $300-1,000 band -- takes the equity book from a 0.02-point breach to a 9.4-point one. The book could then reopen only if equity value FELL to ~$1,280 (a further 32% drawdown) or ~$500 of equity were sold.

_CROSS_BOOK_CASH_COUPLING.what_it_changes: NOT a bar on options entries: the floor governs equity sizing, and reading it as an options gate would double-count the sleeve in the opposite direction and freeze both books. It changes the HONEST COST stated at decision time. During the Aug-Oct posture, price an options entry as 'premium at risk PLUS N points of equity-book floor, extending the equity closure' and put that in the pre-trade checklist.
_CROSS_BOOK_CASH_COUPLING.GUARD: The arithmetic runs backwards and a future run under floor pressure WILL notice: closing the SPY 700P hedge adds ~$532 of cash and lifts the floor 44.98% -> 52.36%, instantly reopening the equity book. DO NOT. That is liquidating insurance to satisfy an accounting ratio. The hedge is exempt from every mechanical exit precisely because its job is to be there when the ratio is not the problem, and its roll/close decision belongs to Ryan under the standing carve-out. Written down explicitly so it is recognised as tempting and refused, not re-derived as clever.
_CROSS_BOOK_CASH_COUPLING.honest_scope: Changed NO decision on the day it was found -- the TACTICAL price clause never fired and CORE had no candidate, so nothing was declined on its strength and nothing licensed by it. That is the only condition under which the desk can audit its own capital rules credibly, and it is why this was written now: the run that finds this while wanting to place a trade is the run least able to weigh it.

_FRIDAY_THETA_COLLAPSES_THE_STOP.claim: On a FRIDAY, weekend theta does to a near-dated TACTICAL position exactly what a LATE ENTRY does -- it collapses the -30% stop back ONTO the trigger level, so the position can no longer be wrong about timing without being wrong about thesis. The late-entry detector prices the stop against an ENTRY that is too high and is therefore computable at entry; THIS defect is not present at entry and arrives purely through the clock, so that detector cannot see it.
_FRIDAY_THETA_COLLAPSES_THE_STOP.the_mechanism: The TACTICAL hard time stop is written in SESSIONS ('flat by the close of the next session'); theta is charged in CALENDAR days. A Friday entry therefore spans 3 calendar days to its time stop and a Tuesday entry spans 1 -- THE SAME RULE COSTS 3x THE THETA on nothing but the weekday.

(a) Treat a Friday near-dated TACTICAL entry as STRICTLY SAME-SESSION: take it only when the +20% target is reachable before the bell, and close at the bell rather than carrying. (b) If it must be carriable, step out to ~21 DTE -- 2.7x less weekend theta -- accepting lower delta and ~45% more capital. the_gap_half_measured_1900Z.the_correction_and_it_points_the_OTHER_W: THE 2026-08-28T15:35Z WEEKEND-GAP FINDING DOES NOT GENERALIZE FROM AN INDEX TO A SINGLE NAME, AND ON NVDA IT INVERTS. Measured, NVDA |open - prior close| by weekday of the open, 2026-06-01..2026-08-27: MONDAY (weekend) n=12, mean 0.948% / median 0.672% / p90 1.524%; TUE-FRI (overnight) n=49, mean 1.222% / median 1.054% / p90 2.255%. Weekend/overnight = 0.78x mean, 0.64x median -- NVDA's weekend gap is SMALLER than its overnight gap, against SPY's 1.36x/1.23x. The mechanism is that a single name's SCHEDULED EVENTS fall on weekdays (the 6.296% maximum in the Tue-Fri sample is the 08-27 earnings gap), so on an event-carrying name the weekday split is dominated by where the events land, not by the calendar. An index has no idiosyncratic print and so shows the clean weekend-premium effect.
the_gap_half_measured_1900Z.why_the_conclusion_SURVIVES_the_inversio: The danger was never that weekends are especially violent on NVDA -- it is that THREE DAYS OF 7-DTE THETA MAKES THE STOP SO SMALL THAT AN ENTIRELY ORDINARY GAP CLEARS IT. Measured on the 2026-09-04 board at 19:03Z, quoted not modelled: 215P mid 3.015 (2.32% of mid, delta -0.394, theta -0.2790, OI 6,038) -> 3-day theta -27.4% of premium, residual stop 0.091% of NVDA; 217.5P mid 4.125 (1.21%, delta -0.488, theta -0.2846, OI 1,882) -> -20.6%, residual stop 0.368%; 220P mid 5.525 (0.90%, delta -0.583, theta -0.2772, OI 14,613) -> -15.0%, residual stop 0.657%. Against the Monday sample those stops are exceeded by the gap ALONE on 12/12 (100%), 8/12 (67%) and 7/12 (58%) of Mondays -- INCLUDING the quiet ones, whose 0.210% minimum still clears the 215P. The +20% target, by contrast, is reached by the gap alone on only 2/12 (17%) in EITHER direction. The asymmetry is not in the gap distribution; it is manufactured by theta shrinking one exit and not the other.
the_gap_half_measured_1900Z.the_generalized_rule: THE HAZARD IS THE THETA-SHRUNKEN STOP, NOT THE WEEKEND -- so state it as a ratio and it applies to every carry, weeknights included. Before carrying any near-dated TACTICAL position through ANY close, compute the residual stop distance in UNDERLYING PERCENT after charging the carry's theta, and compare it to the name's own median gap for that weekday. If the median gap exceeds the residual stop, the position is not stop-managed across the close -- it is a coin flip whose typical outcome is the stop. On NVDA at 7 DTE the median OVERNIGHT gap (1.054%) exceeds all three residual stops too, so a Tuesday carry fails this test as well; the weekend is merely the worst case, at 3x the theta.

NOT an argument to widen the volume or liquidity gates. NOT an excuse to be reached for on a run whose setup actually was marginal -- it applies only where every other gate demonstrably passed, and the run must show that it did.
_CONFIRMATION_LATENCY_VS_RUN_CADENCE.the_strategic_consequence: A desk firing every 15 minutes can reliably participate in setups whose ENTRY WINDOW is measured in hours and cannot reliably participate in ones measured in minutes. Prefer setups where the level itself is the entry and waits for you -- CORE swings, and mean-reversion AT a level -- over breakouts THROUGH a level, where the entry is a moving target that leaves without you. The cadence is Ryan's to change (the trigger config is his, per the CLAUDE.md heartbeat/cadence rules); the desk can only measure it and adapt what it hunts.
_CONFIRMATION_LATENCY_VS_RUN_CADENCE.falsifiable_prediction: Record trigger-to-extremum duration on EVERY future TACTICAL fire. The prediction: fires whose move completes inside ~15 minutes are systematically unreachable; fires that grind for 30+ minutes are reachable. If a sub-15-minute break is ever captured cleanly at a good price, this mechanism is wrong and should be struck.

_CONFIRMED_TRIGGERS_HAVE_A_SHELF_LIFE.claim: A CONFIRMED TRIGGER HAS A SHELF LIFE. The confirmation clause is evaluated AT THE BREAK BAR and says nothing about the minutes after it. On a 15-minute cadence the trigger a run evaluates is routinely 5-20 minutes stale by the time it could be acted on, and for a TACTICAL scalp -- whose whole edge is a level defining a CHEAP invalidation -- that staleness is exactly what converts a good entry into a chase.
_CONFIRMED_TRIGGERS_HAVE_A_SHELF_LIFE.the_arithmetic: retrace_pct = (current - break_extreme) / (trigger - break_extreme), computed AT THE MOMENT OF ENTRY, not at the moment of the trigger. Above ~50% the break is failing and the entry is a chase whatever the trigger did: the invalidation has moved close enough that the position cannot be wrong about timing without being wrong about thesis.

_BREAKOUTS_HAVE_THREE_STATES.claim: A CONFIRMED BREAKOUT HAS THREE OUTCOMES -- EXTEND, FAIL, STALL -- AND EVERY GATE THIS DESK HAS WRITTEN ENCODES ONLY TWO. _BREAKOUTS_HAVE_THREE_STATES.the_rule: Classify a confirmed break on COMPLETED bars, never on the instantaneous print. EXTENDING = still making new extremes OR still trading at/above its break-bar rate. FAILING = the retrace gate trips. STALLED = neither -- no new extremum for N bars AND participation back at or below the PRE-BREAK baseline. STALL IS A DECLINE. Source the third state from PARTICIPATION, not from price: over the exact window where the price reading flickered four times, the volume reading pointed one way for six straight bars. That asymmetry is the whole argument.

What is added is a STATE the gate could not represent -- identified because its first live application returned PASS on a break the desk would obviously decline, a construction defect visible without reference to any outcome. _EVENT_PREMIUM_IS_INVISIBLE_ON_THE_30DTE.claim: THE IV METHOD'S FIXED ~30-DTE BOARD IS STRUCTURALLY BLIND TO A SCHEDULED EVENT INSIDE ~7 DAYS, AND THE EX-GAP RATIO IS NOT A SUBSTITUTE DETECTOR BECAUSE IT MOVES ON ITS DENOMINATOR. Measured four calendar days before AVGO's 2026-09-02 print: the 28-DTE row this desk logs daily shows atm_iv 0.507981 on 2026-08-21 and 0.507981 on 2026-08-28 -- IDENTICAL TO SIX DECIMALS across five sessions -- so read from iv_history.json alone AVGO looks like a name with no event pending. the_measurement_1822Z.method: ATM IV = mean of the ATM call and put IV at one shared strike, quoted (never modelled), same strike on both boards, both boards spanning the 09-02 print.

_EVENT_PREMIUM_IS_INVISIBLE_ON_THE_30DTE.why_the_controls_matter: The obvious objection is that front boards simply always carry more IV, so a 1.49x kink proves nothing. THE CONTROLS REFUTE IT: on a no-event name the term structure runs the OTHER WAY -- SPY's front board is 0.8729x its 28-DTE board (ordinary contango). NVDA, whose print resolved 2026-08-26, sits at 1.0746x, having collapsed from the 1.84x pre-print kink this file already records. Three names, one method, a monotonic ordering that tracks event proximity: 0.87 (none) < 1.07 (just passed) < 1.49 (four days out).
_EVENT_PREMIUM_IS_INVISIBLE_ON_THE_30DTE.the_mechanism_which_makes_it_predictable: Variance is additive in time. A board's total variance is roughly base_vol^2 * T + V_event, and V_event is the SAME absolute quantity on every board that spans the event. So the event's contribution to quoted IV scales like 1/T: on a 7-day board it is spread over 7 days, on a 28-day board over 28. THE EVENT DOES NOT DISAPPEAR FROM THE 28-DTE BOARD -- IT IS DILUTED TO ROUGHLY A QUARTER OF ITS FRONT-BOARD LIFT, which is small enough to hide inside ordinary week-to-week IV noise. That is exactly what happened here.

solving_the_two_boards_gives_the_numbers.arithmetic: base_vol^2 = (var_back - var_front) / ((T2-T1)/365); V_event = var_front - base_vol^2*(T1/365); implied 1-day event move = sqrt(V_event).
solving_the_two_boards_gives_the_numbers.AVGO: base vol 38.12% (NOT the 49.5% or 50.8% headline), implied event move +/-8.74% on the 09-02 print.
solving_the_two_boards_gives_the_numbers.NVDA: base vol 32.27%, residual event +/-2.09% -- i.e. essentially nothing left, which is the correct answer for a print that already happened.
solving_the_two_boards_gives_the_numbers.SPY: base vol 12.00%, V_event NEGATIVE (-0.0000812). The method correctly returns 'no event' rather than a small false positive -- the strongest evidence that it is measuring an event and not a fitting artifact.

_DIVERSIFICATION_STATISTICS_ARE_FRAGILE.the_mechanism: A 30-sample window cannot separate a name's market sensitivity from two idiosyncratic events inside it, and single-name equities gap on news far more often than an index does. So a beta computed over one month of daily bars on a four-name book is dominated by whichever names happened to have catalysts in the window. This is EXACTLY the artifact the IV method already corrects for with rv_30d_ex_top2 -- the desk built the correction, applied it only to volatility, and never asked whether the same window flaw contaminates the OTHER statistic it computes from the same 30 bars.
_DIVERSIFICATION_STATISTICS_ARE_FRAGILE.what_this_does_and_does_not_license: It does NOT say the true betas are higher, lower, or that the book is secretly correlated -- ex-top2 is itself a crude estimator that UNDERSTATES fat-tail risk, exactly as the IV method's own note says, and dropping a real gap can bias either direction. The claim is strictly about ESTIMATE FRAGILITY: three of four numbers move by more than half their magnitude on the removal of two observations, so neither the raw nor the trimmed figure should be quoted as though it were known. Read them as a PAIR, the same way the IV ratios are read.

_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-31.cross_measurement_of_the_tape: CONCURRENT-RUN CROSS-MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-31, AND IT IS THE MOST DIRECT EVIDENCE THIS FILE HAS THAT AN OPENING-WINDOW REGIME LABEL IS NOT A LABEL. Two scheduled runs measured the same tape THREE MINUTES APART and produced OPPOSITE verdicts from CORRECT numbers. 13:36Z (sibling): AMD 475.22 +2.07%, AVGO 371.64 +0.77%, NVDA 218.75 +0.55% -> 'SEMI-LED RISK-ON UNDER A RED INDEX'. 13:38-13:40Z (this run): AMD 467.40 +0.39%, AVGO 367.005 -0.48%, NVDA 217.19 -0.17% -> 'BROAD-BASED RISK-OFF, FINANCIALS-LED'. Neither is wrong: the semis simply FADED between the two reads -- AMD -1.65%, AVGO -1.25%, NVDA -0.71% in about three minutes, while SPY was roughly unchanged (765.77 -> 766.28). || THE LESSON, which extends the 2026-08-28 mid-event finding from an event tape to the ORDINARY OPEN: hand forward the NUMBERS, never the VERDICT. A directional label extracted from the first ten minutes measures whichever leg happened to be running when the run fired, and a later run inheriting it will reason from a frame the tape has already withdrawn. Both labels above should be read as timestamped observations, and any run after ~14:15Z must RE-MEASURE all legs before using either. || The IV readings, by contrast, CROSS-VALIDATE cleanly across the same gap -- SPY 0.120998 vs 0.121370 (0.3% apart), QQQ 0.175312 vs 0.178442 (1.8%), NVDA 0.328571 vs 0.324473 (1.2%), on slightly different ATM strikes. Implied vol was stable while spot direction inverted; that asymmetry is itself the point.

_OPENING_WINDOW_IV_DECAYS_WITH_TIME.headline: THE OPENING-WINDOW ATM INFLATION IS CONFIRMED A FIFTH, SIXTH AND SEVENTH TIME IN DIRECTION -- BUT IT DECAYS WITH TIME, AND A ~20-MINUTE RE-MEASURE CAPTURES ONLY A THIRD TO A HALF OF IT. A RUN THAT RE-QUOTES EARLY HAS NOT FULLY DISCHARGED THE CAVEAT.
_OPENING_WINDOW_IV_DECAYS_WITH_TIME.method: Re-quoted the SAME strike and SAME expiry as each opening-window row, so this measures the artifact and not strike skew. SPY 767 2026-09-30, QQQ 717 2026-09-30, NVDA 220 2026-10-02; call/put averaged per the IV method.
_OPENING_WINDOW_IV_DECAYS_WITH_TIME.the_refinement: The four documented settles -- SPY -2.53%, QQQ -4.37%, NVDA -3.56%, and the 2026-08-27 audit's -4.23% -- were ALL taken 1 to 2 HOURS after the opening print. Today's three were taken ~20-25 minutes after, and came in at -0.60% to -1.95%: same direction, roughly a third to a half the magnitude. The honest mechanism is that the artifact BLEEDS OFF over the session rather than clearing at a threshold, so the size of the correction is a function of how long you waited.
_OPENING_WINDOW_IV_DECAYS_WITH_TIME.consequence: Do not treat 'I re-quoted after 14:00Z' as equivalent to 'this reading is settled'. State the GAP between the opening print and the re-measure when discharging the caveat, because that gap predicts how much of the artifact is still in the number. A row re-measured 20 minutes out is settled enough to stop being an upper bound, but a mid-session re-measure would likely read lower still.
_OPENING_WINDOW_IV_DECAYS_WITH_TIME.honest_scope: CHANGED NO DECISION -- no trade was taken in either book this run and no IV reading was load-bearing, which is the only condition under which a filter's inputs can be audited credibly. n=3 on one morning at one interval; the time-decay shape is inferred from two clusters of readings, not fitted. Do not convert it into a decay curve.
_OPENING_WINDOW_IV_DECAYS_WITH_TIME.what_it_does_not_license: Nothing. All three names read fair-to-cheap on the raw ratio and SPY reads RICH ex-gap at 1.2024. IV sanity is a NECESSARY condition and never a thesis -- fair vol supplies no reason whatsoever to own anything, and CORE still declines on the print cluster.

_REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN.headline: THE EQUITY REPORT'S FIRST FIRE OF THE DAY IS 30 MINUTES AFTER THE BELL, SO THE AUTOMATION'S FIRST-POST-OPEN RUN -- THE ONE THAT TAKES THE DAY'S FIRST AUTONOMOUS EQUITY ENTRY -- ALWAYS ACTS ON THE PREVIOUS SESSION'S REPORT. THIS IS A SCHEDULE MISALIGNMENT, NOT A BUG IN EITHER SYSTEM.
_REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN.evidence: stock-report.yml drives its cadence EXTERNALLY from cron-job.org via workflow_dispatch on 'a single hourly job (~9:00-14:00 CT, Mon-Fri)'. 09:00 CT = 14:00 UTC; the bell is 13:30 UTC. Today's first dispatch fired at 14:00:09Z, exactly on that schedule. The in-repo 'schedule:' entry (cron '0 13 * * 1-5') is documented in the workflow itself as a once-daily SAFETY NET only, and GitHub cron is best-effort -- Friday's scheduled run was created 2026-08-28T22:57:18Z, roughly ten hours late, which is precisely the 'minutes-to-hours late' the workflow's own comment warns about.
_REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN.what_it_meant_today: The last COMPLETED report before this session was run 414, header '2026-08-28 22:59 UTC'. The automation's first-post-open run fired 13:38-13:50Z and placed MMM at 13:37:54Z off that Friday-night report. Run 415 dispatched at 14:00:09Z and its report ('2026-08-31 14:02 UTC') landed on master at ~14:15Z -- so the fresh report existed only from ~45 minutes after the bell.
_REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN.is_it_a_violation: NO, AND DO NOT RETROSPECTIVELY TREAT THE MMM ENTRY AS ONE. v8 bars autonomous equity trades on a STALE report, and a report built on the last COMPLETED session's close is the correct signal basis for a Connors RSI2 daily-bar mean-reversion screen -- Monday morning has no new daily bar yet. What IS a session stale is the report's PRICE column and the entry/stop/target levels derived from it, and its [ERN] earnings annotations, which cannot see a date announced or moved over a weekend. CLAUDE.md already requires sanity-checking the earnings date on any name about to be bought, so the guard exists.
_REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN.the_open_question_for_ryan: Should the first-post-open run be allowed to take an autonomous equity entry off the prior session's report at all, or should it wait for the day's first fresh report? No run has ever made that call explicitly, which is why it is being surfaced rather than decided here. AN UNATTENDED RUN CANNOT ANSWER IT -- HARD RULE 9.
_REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN.the_clean_fix_which_is_RYANS_TO_MAKE: Move cron-job.org's first hourly report fire from 09:00 CT to ~08:15-08:30 CT (13:15-13:30 UTC) so a same-session report exists BEFORE the automation's first-post-open run acts. Agents cannot edit the cron-job.org job, same class as the 2026-08-18 trigger outage. A second, weaker option is to rely on the 13:00Z GitHub backstop, but Friday's ten-hour-late fire is direct evidence it cannot be relied on for timing.
_REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN.detector_for_future_runs: Before any autonomous equity entry, read the report HEADER TIMESTAMP and state it explicitly against the current trading day. If the header predates today's bell, say so in the journal and treat the price/stop/target levels as one session stale even when the signal set is sound.
_REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN._correction_do_not_inherit_the_hung_clai: An earlier draft of this key, written at 14:08Z, said run 415 was 'still in_progress with a frozen updated_at 8+ minutes later', implying a hung workflow. THAT WAS WRONG and is corrected here rather than left standing. The run completed normally and committed. The error came from trusting the GitHub actions list endpoint's status/updated_at fields, which were STALE -- they still read in_progress well after the workflow had finished and pushed. DETECTOR: confirm a workflow's completion by looking for its COMMIT on master, not by polling the actions API's status field. Same shape as this file's other measurement bugs -- a convenient indicator was trusted over the primary artifact.
_REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN.scope_note: The 30-minute gap is the durable finding and is UNAFFECTED by the correction above: cron-job.org's first fire is 09:00 CT = 14:00 UTC against a 13:30 UTC bell, verified from the workflow's own documented schedule and from today's 14:00:09Z dispatch. Report generation then takes ~2 minutes plus commit time.

_HOLE_CORRUPTED_THE_PRICE_CLAUSE_FLATTER.headline: A FEED HOLE HID THE BREAK LEVEL ITSELF, TURNING A BREAK THAT ROUND-TRIPPED INSIDE ITS OWN BAR INTO AN APPARENT CLEAN HOLD. This file documents holes hiding session extremes and depressing volume denominators; this is the first instance where the hidden extreme WAS the trigger level, and the distortion pointed toward taking the trade.
_HOLE_CORRUPTED_THE_PRICE_CLAUSE_FLATTER.the_hole: Cross-symbol signature per the 2026-08-27 rule: the 14:10Z 5-minute bucket was holed SIMULTANEOUSLY on all three symbols measured. NVDA reported 87,672 against a 1-minute sum of 1,057,298 (-91.71%); SPY 6,907 against 120,938 (-94.29%); QQQ 17,436 against 138,954 (-87.45%). Per the 2026-08-28 DIRECTION rule the bucket is materially BELOW its 1-minute sum in every case, so the BUCKET is the holed side and the 1-minute sum substitutes.
_HOLE_CORRUPTED_THE_PRICE_CLAUSE_FLATTER.the_new_part_price_not_volume: NVDA's holed bucket reported OHLC 220.035 / 220.200 / 220.000 / 220.190. The TRUE bucket, rebuilt from its 1-minute constituents, is 219.380 / 220.200 / 219.267 / 220.170. The reported LOW of 220.000 is wrong by 0.733 -- and the true low of 219.267 sits BELOW the 219.6195 session high the break was made through. So the 5-minute series portrayed price consolidating tightly above the level, when in fact it broke, traded back UNDER the level mid-bucket, and only reclaimed 220 in the final minute. A run reading the 5-minute series alone would have scored 'held beyond the level' as satisfied. It was not.
_HOLE_CORRUPTED_THE_PRICE_CLAUSE_FLATTER.why_it_is_the_dangerous_direction: Same reason an under-reported bucket manufactures volume confirmation: the distortion argues FOR the trade. A holed bucket shows one constituent minute's range, and on an UPSIDE break the minute that survives is disproportionately likely to be the last one -- which is the highest one. The price clause is therefore biased toward false positives on exactly the bars a breakout desk cares about.
_HOLE_CORRUPTED_THE_PRICE_CLAUSE_FLATTER.the_rule: Reconcile the bucket against the 1-minute series BEFORE testing the price clause, not only before computing a volume baseline. The existing detector is unchanged and sufficient; what is new is WHERE to apply it. 'Did it hold beyond the level' is a question about a bar's LOW (on a long) or HIGH (on a short), which is precisely the field a hole destroys.
_HOLE_CORRUPTED_THE_PRICE_CLAUSE_FLATTER.mixed_form_worth_noting: This hole is a MIXED presentation. Its OHLC is byte-for-byte the 14:14 one-minute bar (220.035/220.200/220.000, the single-constituent signature), but its VOLUME of 87,672 matches NO constituent minute (240,529 / 330,209 / 238,852 / 184,587 / 63,121) -- the partial form the 2026-08-28T15:35Z finding recorded. One bucket can be single-constituent in price and partial in volume at once, so neither signature alone is the test. The reconciliation GAP remains the test.
_HOLE_CORRUPTED_THE_PRICE_CLAUSE_FLATTER.honest_scope: Changed no decision. The trade was independently declined on index disagreement and on the volume clause, and the price clause was incomplete anyway (the holding bar had not closed). A feed-integrity finding is only creditable when the audit does not license a trade.
_HOLE_CORRUPTED_THE_PRICE_CLAUSE_FLATTER.FOLLOW_UP_2026-08-31T14:27Z_HOLES_DO_NOT: Re-fetched at 14:27Z, SEVENTEEN MINUTES after the bar closed: the 14:10Z 5-minute bucket STILL reports 87,672 against a 1,081,849 one-minute sum (-91.9%), OHLC still byte-for-byte the 14:14 minute, still hiding the true bucket low of 219.2672. THE RULE THIS ADDS: the 2026-08-26 'fetch the window twice a few minutes apart' detector catches PROVISIONAL bars, NOT holes -- a second identical read is NOT evidence a bucket is clean. Only the 1-minute reconciliation settles a hole. Control, so this is a hole and not a systematic offset: the 14:15Z bucket reads 1,185,159 vs a 1,156,642 one-minute sum (+2.5%) and the 14:20Z bucket 1,179,206 vs 1,136,656 (+3.7%), both inside tolerance. Separately the 1-MINUTE series was itself revised UP -- this run's break-bar sum 1,081,849 vs the 14:20Z run's 1,057,298 (+2.3%), the 2026-08-26 provisional-bar finding -- moving the break bar from 92.8% to 94.9% of baseline and changing nothing.

_NVDA_BREAK_DECLINED_ON_TAPE_NOT_VEHICLE.headline: RESOLVED 14:27Z -- THE PRICE CLAUSE COMPLETED AND PASSED, VOLUME MARGINALLY PASSED, AND THE BREAK FAILED ANYWAY IN FIVE MINUTES. INDEX DISAGREEMENT WAS THE LONE DISSENTING GATE AND THE ONLY ONE THAT WAS RIGHT. Original 14:18Z headline, retained: the least overdetermined TACTICAL decline this desk has logged on the long side -- the vehicle is excellent, the late-entry arithmetic PASSES, the catalyst screen PASSES; the decline rested on trigger quality and index disagreement.
_NVDA_BREAK_DECLINED_ON_TAPE_NOT_VEHICLE.the_trigger: NVDA broke its 219.6195 session high (set 14:08Z) with a completed 5-minute close at 220.170 in the 14:10-14:14Z bucket, spot 220.17 at 14:16Z, +1.19% on the day against a red tape. _NVDA_BREAK_DECLINED_ON_TAPE_NOT_VEHICLE.veto_1_price_clause_incomplete: The clause requires a completed close beyond the level AND holding beyond it on the FOLLOWING bar. At 14:18Z the 14:15-14:19Z bar was still open. One leg satisfied, one pending. _NVDA_BREAK_DECLINED_ON_TAPE_NOT_VEHICLE.veto_2_volume_does_not_confirm_and_is_ba: Corrected break-bar volume 1,057,298 (the reported 87,672 is holed). _NVDA_BREAK_DECLINED_ON_TAPE_NOT_VEHICLE.veto_3_index_disagreement_the_decisive_o: v8 TACTICAL requires the index tape agreeing. At 14:16Z: NVDA 220.095 +1.17% at session highs, against SPY 765.76 -0.467% and QQQ 714.11 -0.324%, both ranging near session lows and both BELOW their 20-day SMAs (769.216 / 717.942) for the entire session. The counter-reading -- rotation into quality leadership -- is available and is NOT dismissed; it is simply not what the clause asks for.

PANW/DELL/CRDO/MDB print 09-01 pm and AVGO/SNOW/HPE/NTAP 09-02 pm -- ALL AFTER that bell, hence OUTSIDE this track's window while sitting inside every CORE window. _NVDA_BREAK_DECLINED_ON_TAPE_NOT_VEHICLE.the_handoff_numbers_not_a_verdict: Per the 2026-08-31 concurrent-run lesson, what follows is timestamped observation, not a frame to inherit. The setup becomes live if, on a LATER bar: the 14:15-14:19Z or a subsequent 5-minute bar closes above 219.62 AND the next bar holds above it; participation on that two-bar window clears the then-current baselines (re-derive them, and by then a post-first-hour baseline will exist and should be used); and SPY/QQQ stop making session lows. Any run acting on this MUST re-derive all three -- the level, the baseline, and the index legs -- off freshly reconciled bars.
_NVDA_BREAK_DECLINED_ON_TAPE_NOT_VEHICLE.resolution_price_clause_PASSED: The 14:15-14:19Z holding bar closed and the clause is now testable. BREAK BAR (14:10-14:14Z, rebuilt from 1-minute constituents because the bucket is holed): completed close 220.190, above the 219.6195 level. HOLDING BAR (14:15-14:19Z): close 220.000 above the level, and its true LOW of 219.700 stayed ABOVE the level for the whole bar -- it held cleanly, not marginally. veto_1 is therefore DISCHARGED: it was correctly recorded as a NOT YET, and the answer turned out to be YES. This is the FIRST break in the arc to satisfy the two-bar price clause on a structural level with no measurement caveat.
_NVDA_BREAK_DECLINED_ON_TAPE_NOT_VEHICLE.resolution_volume_clause_MARGINALLY_PASS: Evaluated over the SAME two-bar window per the 2026-08-28 construction fix. Trailing-30 local mean (13:40-14:09Z, six buckets) = 1,139,556. Break bar 1,081,849 = 94.9%; holding bar 1,156,642 = 101.5%. Against the ex-open session mean (1,185,011): 91.3% / 97.6%. The holding bar CLEARS the trailing-30 baseline with the break bar not materially below it -- the two-bar confirmation condition. That baseline is drawn entirely from first-hour buckets, which per 2026-08-25 is the INFLATED too-strict mode, so 101.5% understates rather than flatters. veto_2 ('does not confirm and is not confidently readable') was the honest call on the data then available, and resolves to a marginal PASS on the completed window.
_NVDA_BREAK_DECLINED_ON_TAPE_NOT_VEHICLE.resolution_the_outcome: The 14:20-14:24Z bucket closed 219.550 -- BELOW the 219.6195 trigger. Live spot 219.625 at 14:27Z, sitting exactly ON the level. The confirmed break fully round-tripped in FIVE MINUTES. Index disagreement (veto_3) meanwhile DEEPENED on every leg: SPY -0.593% (was -0.467%), QQQ -0.445% (was -0.324%), XLF -0.576%, IWM -0.913%, all at or near session lows, against NVDA +0.953% and SMH +0.391%.
_NVDA_BREAK_DECLINED_ON_TAPE_NOT_VEHICLE.WHY_THIS_ONE_IS_CITABLE: FIRST BREAK IN THE ARC WHERE THE GATES DISAGREED WITH EACH OTHER, so the outcome adjudicates BETWEEN them instead of confirming them jointly. Every prior failure was overdetermined -- several gates failing together, or the 2026-08-26 regime capstone applying. The capstone explicitly does NOT apply here: the 14:20Z run established that the 09-01 pm / 09-02 pm print cluster falls entirely OUTSIDE a TACTICAL window flat by the 09-01 bell, and refused to borrow CORE's objection. So this failure is NOT 'a breakout into an unresolved catalyst'. Price passed, volume marginally passed, index disagreement was the lone dissent -- and the lone dissent was right.
_NVDA_BREAK_DECLINED_ON_TAPE_NOT_VEHICLE.THE_CLAIM_AT_ITS_HONEST_STRENGTH: n=1, and this must NOT be written forward as though one break established that the index-agreement clause carries edge. What it is: the first observation in this arc that DISCRIMINATES between the gates rather than confirming them together, and it points OPPOSITE to the tuning arc's instinct. The desk has spent five sessions refining the volume denominator through four distinct correction modes (session-average too strict, trailing-local too easy in decay, closing-auction too easy, post-flush too strict). The gate that would have made THIS call is the one nobody has tuned or measured systematically. Worth a deliberate look before the next denominator refinement.
_NVDA_BREAK_DECLINED_ON_TAPE_NOT_VEHICLE.OPERATIONAL_shelf_life_is_about_one_run: A measured instance of _CONFIRMED_TRIGGERS_HAVE_A_SHELF_LIFE. Confirmation completed 14:19Z; the break was dead by 14:24Z -- FIVE MINUTES, which at this cadence is roughly ONE RUN. A trigger confirmed by the run that observes it may already be dead before the next run could act on it. Any TACTICAL entry off a confirmed break must be placed by the run that confirms it, or re-confirmed from scratch -- NEVER inherited as a standing trigger.
_NVDA_BREAK_DECLINED_ON_TAPE_NOT_VEHICLE.honest_scope: CHANGED NO DECISION. Declined at 14:20Z, still declined, and spot has round-tripped so there is nothing to take -- an entry now would be a re-entry into a failed break, not a late entry. A gate audit is only credible on a run the audit does not license a trade for.

RESOLVED_2026-08-31T14:35Z.outcome: THE BREAK FAILED. All three conditions this key handed forward were tested on fresh bars and the setup is DEAD as written -- the 219.6195 level is now chop, not a trigger.
RESOLVED_2026-08-31T14:35Z.price_clause_completed_then_decayed: It PASSED: 14:10 bucket closed 220.190 and 14:15 closed 220.000, both above 219.6195, so the two-bar clause was satisfied as of 14:19Z. Then 14:20 closed 219.550 -- BELOW the level on a completed close -- and 14:25 reclaimed at 220.075. Three crossings of the trigger in twenty minutes. Twenty-five minutes on, NVDA sits 220.065: +0.45 (+0.20%) above the trigger and BELOW its 220.360 session high.
RESOLVED_2026-08-31T14:35Z.THE_TRANSFERABLE_PART: First fire in this arc where the two-bar price clause COMPLETED and the level was then LOST on a LATER completed close. The clause is a two-bar test and is silent about bar three -- not a defect, a filter must stop looking somewhere -- but it means a satisfied price clause is a NECESSARY CONDITION THAT EXPIRES, not a state that persists. Never inherit 'the price clause passed' from an earlier run as still-true; re-test it on current bars, the same discipline the 2026-08-25 stale-box finding demands for the numbers inside the clause.

(This key's 1,057,298 differs by +2.3%: ordinary one-minute post-close revision per the 2026-08-26 finding, inside tolerance.) Two-bar window: break 1,081,849, hold 1,185,159. Trailing-30 (six buckets 13:40-14:09) 1,157,093 -> 93.5% / 102.4%. Session bucket rate (twelve buckets, corrected) 1,305,606 -> 82.9% / 90.8%. Break bar fails the trailing local; BOTH fail the session rate. Stated against my own conclusion: no post-first-hour baseline existed yet, so the trailing-30 is still the opening-inflated too-strict mode -- but the session-rate leg fails independently of that.

SPY printed its session low 764.7205 at 14:25Z and QQQ its 713.160 at 14:26Z -- inside the six minutes before measurement. _RESERVE_IS_THE_STRICTER_OF_TWO.headline: EVERY RUN SINCE THE 2026-08-29 CAPITAL AMENDMENT HAS QUOTED DEPLOYABLE CAPITAL FROM THE 5%-OF-TOTAL RESERVE ALONE, WHILE FOUR LAWS #4's FLAT $250 SAT UNAPPLIED BESIDE IT AND IS STRICTER AT THIS ACCOUNT SIZE.
_RESERVE_IS_THE_STRICTER_OF_TWO.the_arithmetic: CLAUDE.md's full-deployment policy sets an operational reserve of 5% of total_value, recomputed each run: 0.05 x $3,973.02 = $198.65. FOUR LAWS #4 says 'Always leave >=$250 unencumbered.' The governance rule is 'where either is stricter, the stricter rule applies'. $250 > $198.65, so the binding reserve is $250 and deployable = $1,046.96 - $250 = $796.96, NOT the $848.45 the 14:05Z and 14:15Z runs quoted (they used $848.45 off a $198.51 reserve). Overstatement today: $51.35.
_RESERVE_IS_THE_STRICTER_OF_TWO.the_crossover_and_why_it_will_not_self_c: The two rules agree only at 0.05 x total = 250, i.e. a total_value of $5,000. BELOW $5,000 the flat $250 binds; above it the 5% formula does. This account has been below $5,000 for the entire life of the full-deployment policy, so the 5% formula has been the wrong number every single time it has been quoted, and will stay wrong until the account grows ~26%. It is a permanent-until-fixed error, not a transient one.

_LATE_ENTRY_COST_ON_A_FLAT_UNDERLYING.headline: THE LATE-ENTRY DETECTOR MEASURED FOR THE FIRST TIME ON A MOTIONLESS UNDERLYING, WHICH ISOLATES THE COST OF MERELY WAITING: an 11-DTE ATM tactical vehicle bled -2.46% in fourteen minutes while its underlying moved -0.048%.
_LATE_ENTRY_COST_ON_A_FLAT_UNDERLYING.why_the_test_is_new: Both prior tests (2026-08-28, -11.25% and -11.19%) ran on underlyings that MOVED, so the delta term dominated and the non-delta cost could not be separated. Holding spot nearly fixed separates it.
_LATE_ENTRY_COST_ON_A_FLAT_UNDERLYING.what_it_says: Delta accounts for roughly -0.055 and theta roughly -0.002 across fourteen minutes. About HALF the loss is neither -- implied-vol bleed plus a bid/ask that DOUBLED from 0.99% to 2.02% of mid. Order of magnitude: ~1.2-1.4% of premium per quarter-hour to hold an 11-DTE ATM tactical contract with the underlying standing still, against a +20% target needing only ~+1.04% on NVDA. THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: 'why NOW' is not a stylistic gate on a scalp, it is the arithmetic -- a tactical thesis that needs half an hour to be right has already spent a quarter of its target.
_LATE_ENTRY_COST_ON_A_FLAT_UNDERLYING.limits_stated_plainly: n=1. The prior run did not record this contract's IV, so the vol-versus-spread split is INFERRED from the residual, not measured -- do not quote the decomposition finer than 'roughly half'. Part of the spread widening may be quote timing rather than a real liquidity change. It changed no decision (the trade was declined on three other grounds and stays declined), which is the only condition under which a detector can be audited credibly.

_HANDOFF_CONJUNCTIONS_CLEAR_OUT_OF_ORDER.finding: A handoff that lists conditions as a conjunction invites the next run to read partial satisfaction as partial progress. It is not. Measured on the 14:35Z NVDA handoff's three conditions: condition 3 (index legs no longer printing session lows) CLEARED -- SPY's 764.721 low was set 14:25Z and QQQ's 713.160 at 14:26Z, neither renewed in ~20 minutes. Condition 1 (a completed 5-minute close above the structural level, next bar holding) FAILED OUTRIGHT: NVDA extended its session high to 220.600 on a WICK but never closed a bucket above 220.360, the highest completed close being 220.175. The volume condition was never reached.
_HANDOFF_CONJUNCTIONS_CLEAR_OUT_OF_ORDER.the_mechanism: The three gates have wildly different costs to clear. An index leg ceasing to make new lows is satisfied by ordinary mean reversion and demands nothing whatsoever of the setup; a completed close through a level on real participation is the only one carrying information. So the cheap gate cleared, the decisive one did not, and a run counting satisfied gates would feel two-thirds of the way to a trade while being no closer at all.
_HANDOFF_CONJUNCTIONS_CLEAR_OUT_OF_ORDER.the_rule: WHEN HANDING FORWARD A CONJUNCTION, RANK THE CONDITIONS BY WHAT THEY COST TO CLEAR AND NAME WHICH IS DECISIVE. Otherwise the COUNT of satisfied gates gets mistaken for PROXIMITY to a setup -- and the count rises fastest on the gates that mean least.
_HANDOFF_CONJUNCTIONS_CLEAR_OUT_OF_ORDER.robustness: Measured on BOTH bar constructions: the broker's 5-minute buckets and an independent rebuild from the 1-minute series agree on every close to within 0.015 and both place the 220.600 high inside the 14:35 bucket. Two constructions, one answer.
_HANDOFF_CONJUNCTIONS_CLEAR_OUT_OF_ORDER.honest_scope: Changed no decision -- the trade was declined on the price clause alone and would have been whatever the index legs did. A gate-ordering audit is only creditable on a run where it does not license a trade.

The trend-maturity gate's clause (c) -- does the PRESENT tape confirm or diverge -- has been applied name-by-name for nine runs of this session. It is computable across the whole candidate set in one get_equity_quotes call, before any thesis workup, and it answers a question no individual grade can: am I looking for a stabilizing name inside a stabilizing group, or hunting the single exception?
_OVERSOLD_COHORT_IS_MEASURABLE_BEFORE_AN.measured_2026-08-31T15_27Z: 15 non-held RSI2 / oversold-uptrend candidates vs prior close: REGN +0.222 (the ONLY green) | AEHR -0.588 | KLAC -0.644 | IWM -0.872 | COF -0.902 | CAT -1.192 | AMAT -1.224 | RTX -1.445 | TSEM -1.808 | GE -1.870 | MRVL -2.006 | GEV -2.139 | MAR -2.227 | GD -2.291 | BE -2.799. _OVERSOLD_COHORT_IS_MEASURABLE_BEFORE_AN.the_reasoning: An RSI2 mean-reversion entry is a bet that an oversold name STOPS going down. A cohort being distributed at 3.2x the index rate is that bet failing across the class on the day you would take it -- and it explains, in two lines, nine consecutive name-by-name declines.
_OVERSOLD_COHORT_IS_MEASURABLE_BEFORE_AN.the_honest_caveat_which_limits_the_claim: An oversold cohort underperforming on a down day is PARTLY EXPECTED BY CONSTRUCTION: the screen selects names already being sold, skewing the sample toward weakness and high beta. This does NOT prove the setup class is broken and a run reading it that way has over-claimed. What it establishes is narrower and sufficient -- today shows DISTRIBUTION where the entry needs STABILIZATION. Note also that the cohort is not merely high-beta: GD, RTX, CAT and MAR are low-beta names and all four fell 1.2-2.3% against an index down 0.45%.
_OVERSOLD_COHORT_IS_MEASURABLE_BEFORE_AN.how_to_read_the_exception: The single green name is the one worth working -- but relative strength for ONE SESSION is one data point, and it does not repair a weak setup. REGN was that name today and was still declined: spot 795.95 sits only -0.84% below its own 20-day (802.69), so its RSI2 4.6 print comes from five small down days rather than a washout, with very little to revert. Compare the cohort's real washouts: KLAC -9.0%, AMAT -10.3%, GEV -9.8% below their 20-days. Depth of pullback and relative strength are SEPARATE tests and a candidate needs both.
_OVERSOLD_COHORT_IS_MEASURABLE_BEFORE_AN.the_shape_of_the_lesson: Same family as the denominator findings: a statistic every run needed was cheaply computable and nobody computed it, so nine runs re-derived a worse version of it one name at a time. _THE_200DAY_GATE_CERTIFIES_DOWNTRENDS.headline: THE EQUITY REPORT'S 'OVERSOLD WITHIN A RISING 200-DAY UPTREND' GATE PASSED A NAME SITTING BELOW ITS 20-, 50- AND 130-DAY AVERAGES, 16% OFF ITS HIGH, SIX SESSIONS INTO LOWER CLOSES. THE 200-DAY LAGS TOO MUCH TO CERTIFY 'DIP IN AN UPTREND'. ADD THE 50-DAY AS THE DISCRIMINATOR.
_THE_200DAY_GATE_CERTIFIES_DOWNTRENDS.the_demonstration_not_an_inference: MAR was today's best-looking tradeable RSI2 candidate -- RSI2 2.4, the deepest oversold on the list after AEHR, a tight -3.6% suggested stop, no earnings in the window, no sector overlap with the book, non-oil, non-spec. Measured off daily closes: spot 344.03 against 20SMA 354.86, 50SMA 366.86 and a 130-session SMA of 359.17 -- BELOW ALL THREE, with the 50-day sitting ABOVE the 20-day (the classic downtrend stack). 16.3% off the 410.98 window high. Closes 356.39 -> 360.20 -> 357.77 -> 358.67 -> 353.87 -> 351.08 -> 344.03. That is a falling knife the screen certified as a dip in an uptrend.
_THE_200DAY_GATE_CERTIFIES_DOWNTRENDS.the_mechanism: A 200-day SMA averages a full year, so it keeps rising for months after the intermediate trend has rolled over. An RSI2 screen CANNOT fire unless price is stretched below its short-term averages -- that is what oversold means -- so 'below the 20-day' carries no information and every candidate has it. The 50-day is the first average that distinguishes the two cases: above it, there is an established mean above spot for price to revert TOWARD; below it, mean reversion has no mean, and the trade is a bet against an intermediate downtrend.
_THE_200DAY_GATE_CERTIFIES_DOWNTRENDS.applied_to_todays_list: MAR below 20/50/130 -> REJECT. GD spot 371.25 below 20SMA 387.56 AND 50SMA 375.98 -> REJECT on the same test. RTX 208.57 below 20SMA 218.12 but ABOVE 50SMA 205.85 by only 0.64% -> passes narrowly. REGN 793.53 below 20SMA 802.69, above 50SMA 716.62 by 10.7% -> passes clearly. Note GD -2.1% and RTX -1.5% on the same session with both flagged by the same screen is ONE defense-sector move, not two independent ideas -- treat correlated same-day flags as a single candidate.
_THE_200DAY_GATE_CERTIFIES_DOWNTRENDS.the_book_measured_the_same_way_and_the_H: All five held positions were below their 20-day at entry, which confirms the gate carries no information rather than indicting any entry. Split by the 50-day: below 20 ONLY (MDLZ, MMM, LLY) now -0.65% / -0.33% / -2.75%, mean -1.24%; below 20 AND 50 (ROST entry 230.15 vs 20SMA 244.31 / 50SMA 234.44; PNC entry 246.47 vs 252.50 / 247.31) now -1.57% / -2.56%, mean -2.07%. DIRECTIONALLY CONSISTENT WITH THE MECHANISM AND STATISTICALLY WORTHLESS -- n=5, one tape, four sessions, every position underwater because the market has not bounced. This is recorded as a REASON TO ADD A CHEAP GATE, never as evidence the gate works. Do not cite these five numbers as a backtest.
_THE_200DAY_GATE_CERTIFIES_DOWNTRENDS.what_to_do: Before any autonomous equity entry, compute the candidate's 20- and 50-day SMA off daily closes and state both distances. Below the 50-day is not an automatic veto, but it downgrades the setup out of A-grade absent a specific reason the intermediate downtrend is ending -- which under the posture's A-grade-only bar means no entry. It is one get_equity_historicals call the run already needs, and it is the same discipline the TACTICAL track learned on 2026-08-25 (compute BOTH the 20- and 50-day before drawing any level).
_THE_200DAY_GATE_CERTIFIES_DOWNTRENDS.scope_and_what_this_is_NOT: This is a finding about the SCREEN's trend gate, not about report.py being broken -- the report says plainly that entry/stop/target are ESTIMATES and that the signal is purely technical, and HARD RULE 7 already requires a thesis gate on top. The gap this closes is that the thesis gate is a NEWS check, and news would not have caught MAR: there need be no bad headline for a name to be in a six-session downtrend. The trend test is the cheap structural check the stack was missing.
_THE_200DAY_GATE_CERTIFIES_DOWNTRENDS._union_merge_note: UNION MERGE, concurrent same-slot runs 15:25Z and 15:30Z (PR #903 and #904). Both keys are kept because they measure DIFFERENT things and neither subsumes the other: the sibling's _OVERSOLD_COHORT_IS_MEASURABLE_BEFORE_ANY_NAME_IS_GRADED is a TAPE argument -- 14 of 15 flagged names underperformed SPY today, so the whole cohort is falling together right now -- while this key is a STRUCTURAL argument about the screen's trend gate, which holds on any tape and would reject MAR on a green day too. Read them as a pair: the cohort test says whether to hunt this list AT ALL today, and the 50-day test says which members are dips rather than knives. || CROSS-VALIDATION WORTH RECORDING: both runs independently caught the same defect in the 15:15Z structural claim -- that it measured only levels ABOVE spot and missed QQQ's 50-day below. The sibling quoted 2.706 below spot at its timestamp, this run 2.176 at 15:31Z; the gap is spot drift between reads (714.77 vs 714.24), not a disagreement. _TAPE_CONFIRMATION_AND_THE_RSI2_SCREEN_A.claim: THE EVIDENCE THAT SATISFIES TREND-MATURITY CLAUSE (c) IS THE SAME EVENT THAT REMOVES A NAME FROM THE RSI2 SCREEN. Clause (c) demands the PRESENT tape confirm the entry -- for a mean-reversion long that means the name is turning UP. But Connors RSI2 only lists names with RSI2 < 10, and a name turning up is a name whose RSI2 is rising through that gate. A candidate that visibly confirms tends to disqualify itself from the screen that found it, and the window between the two is roughly ONE REPORT CYCLE.

_TAPE_CONFIRMATION_AND_THE_RSI2_SCREEN_A.the_rule: Re-read the freshest committed report on master immediately before placing, exactly as the collision rule already requires for the broker -- a name can leave the screen inside one run. And when a mean-reversion candidate's chief attraction is that it is ALREADY turning, check its RSI2 has not left the gate: that attraction and that disqualification are the same fact measured twice.
_TAPE_CONFIRMATION_AND_THE_RSI2_SCREEN_A.why_this_is_not_an_argument_to_relax_the: The screen is not being pedantic. RSI2 rising through 10 means the oversold condition the strategy exploits has RESOLVED -- the edge is spent, not merely aged. Buying anyway is buying after the trigger, which is the equity-book twin of the TACTICAL late-entry defect already recorded at 2026-08-28T15:05Z. Both say: the level that defines a cheap invalidation is the thing you are paid for, and entering after price has left it spends exactly that.
_TAPE_CONFIRMATION_AND_THE_RSI2_SCREEN_A.the_honest_caveat: This changed the OUTCOME of this run (a fully-worked A-grade candidate was declined), so it is not one of the audits this file prefers -- the ones that change no decision. Stated plainly so the next instance weighs it accordingly: the thesis work on REGN was sound and remains on file; if REGN re-prints RSI2 < 10 on a future report it is a live candidate again and this note is the reason it was passed over, not evidence against it.

_RSI2_SCREEN_TREND_FAILURE_IS_SYSTEMATIC.headline: THE REPORT'S 'RISING 200-DAY' GATE DOES NOT ENFORCE AN UPTREND, AND THE FAILURE IS THE MAJORITY CASE, NOT AN ANECDOTE: 5 OF 8 SCREEN NAMES TESTED SIT BELOW THEIR 20-, 50- AND 130-DAY AVERAGES, FOUR OF THEM 22-42% OFF THEIR HIGHS.
_RSI2_SCREEN_TREND_FAILURE_IS_SYSTEMATIC.supersedes_scope_of: _THE_200DAY_GATE_CERTIFIES_DOWNTRENDS (2026-08-31T15:30Z) recorded ONE name (MAR) whose 200-day gate certified a downtrend as a dip. That finding is CORRECT and is not superseded -- it is GENERALIZED. This run tested the whole screen and found MAR was not an outlier; it was typical.
_RSI2_SCREEN_TREND_FAILURE_IS_SYSTEMATIC.method: Daily closes through 2026-08-28 (get_equity_historicals, interval=day, 145 reg bars from 2026-02-02). For each name: SMA20 / SMA50 / SMA130, % off the highest close in the window, and consecutive lower closes. The 200-day is NOT computable from a 145-bar window and is deliberately not quoted -- the point is that the intermediate averages already settle the question.

measurements.COF: last 215.67 | 20d 219.34 | 50d 210.27 | 130d 197.09 |  -5.1% off high | below 20d ONLY -- genuine pullback
measurements.BLK: last 1164.48 | 20d 1153.30 | 50d 1080.72 | 130d 1045.86 | -1.6% off high | ABOVE ALL THREE -- the only one

_RSI2_SCREEN_TREND_FAILURE_IS_SYSTEMATIC.mechanism: A 200-day average is still rising on year-ago data long after price has broken down. A name 40% off its high can sit above a rising 200-day for months. So the gate as written admits deep downtrends and calls them dips. Connors' RSI(2) mean-reversion is specified for names ABOVE their long-term average and in an intact uptrend; the report's gate does not enforce that in any usable form, and the RSI2 print itself is trend-blind by construction.
_RSI2_SCREEN_TREND_FAILURE_IS_SYSTEMATIC.detector: BEFORE grading any RSI2 name, compute SMA20 / SMA50 / SMA130 and % off high. Below all three = DOWNTREND, decline it -- do not spend a thesis workup on it. This is one get_equity_historicals call for up to 10 names and it disqualified five of eight candidates in a single pass, which is far cheaper than the per-name news-and-analyst workup the gate stack would otherwise demand.
_RSI2_SCREEN_TREND_FAILURE_IS_SYSTEMATIC.the_inversion_that_makes_this_hard: THE TREND FILTER AND THE MEAN-REVERSION EDGE POINT IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, AND THIS IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN A QUIRK OF TODAY. BLK passes the trend test BECAUSE it is only 1.6% off its high -- and that same fact is what makes it the WEAKEST reversion candidate on the screen: there is almost nothing to revert into. Its RSI2 of 5.9 was generated by FOUR CONSECUTIVE SMALL DOWN DAYS (a sequence), not by any magnitude of decline; RSI2 is a 2-day oscillator and prints single digits on a 0.2% slide if the slide is consistent. _COMPLEX_VETOES_NEED_A_MAGNITUDE_TEST.rule_amended: A complex veto now needs BOTH tests. (1) MAGNITUDE: quote the complex ETF, the index, and the ratio -- below ~2x the index it is beta, not a de-rate. (2) DISPERSION: quote the MEMBERS and the best-to-worst spread. If one member is a multi-sigma outlier or any member is GREEN, the ETF number is a weighted average and not a regime, and 'the complex is de-rating' is the wrong description of it. The magnitude test alone cannot tell a de-rating complex from a complex containing one blowup -- both print the same ETF number.

_A_BLOCK_PRINT_INFLATES_THE_BASELINE_AND.headline: FIFTH DENOMINATOR MODE, AND THE FIRST ONE THE FEED-INTEGRITY DETECTORS ARE STRUCTURALLY BLIND TO: a single BLOCK CROSS inflates the trailing-volume baseline ~2.5x for half an hour while moving price ONE CENT. _A_BLOCK_PRINT_INFLATES_THE_BASELINE_AND.effect_on_the_confirmation_clause: Trailing-30 baseline over the six 16:00-16:25Z buckets: RAW 108,766 vs BLOCK-ADJUSTED 43,986 -- the raw denominator is 2.47x the honest one. A genuine break on XLF in the next half hour would have to trade 108,767 to confirm instead of 43,986, so the clause runs ~2.5x too STRICT, set by a print that carried no directional information whatsoever.
_A_BLOCK_PRINT_INFLATES_THE_BASELINE_AND.why_it_is_new_and_why_it_survives_every_: The four modes already recorded (session-average too strict, trailing-local too easy in a decaying tape, closing-auction too easy, post-flush too strict) are all about WHICH WINDOW the baseline is drawn over, and the feed-integrity family (5-min vs 1-min direction rule, cross-symbol agreement, double-fetch) is built to catch volume that is MISSING. This is neither: the window is right and the data is correct to the share. THE DETECTOR FAMILY IS STRUCTURALLY BLIND TO EXCESS VOLUME BECAUSE EXCESS VOLUME IS NOT AN ERROR. Reconciliation reported CLEAN and the denominator was still wrong by 2.5x.
_A_BLOCK_PRINT_INFLATES_THE_BASELINE_AND.the_detector: A 1-minute bar that is a large multiple of BOTH neighbours WITH A PRICE RANGE NEAR ZERO is a block cross, not participation -- exclude it from any trailing baseline used as a confirmation denominator. This is the exact mirror of the existing recognition rule ('a 1-minute bar whose volume is a tiny fraction of both neighbours is provisional'). The discriminator is RANGE, not size: participation moves price, a cross does not.
_A_BLOCK_PRINT_INFLATES_THE_BASELINE_AND.direction_of_error_and_the_case_to_watch: Here it errs STRICT, which is the safe direction -- it vetoes real breaks rather than manufacturing fake ones. THE DANGEROUS CASE IS THE SAME PRINT LANDING ON THE BREAK BAR ITSELF: a block cross inside the two-bar confirmation window would supply the participation the clause is looking for, on a trade that expressed no view at all. Check the break bar's RANGE against its volume before crediting it.

XLF is not a TACTICAL vehicle at this account size and no trigger existed on it or on anything else this run -- SPY spent the hour in a 1.36-point band. _A_DECLINE_THROUGH_POSITIVE_NEWS_IS_STRO.the_general_rule: When a screen name is weak, ask not only HOW MUCH but AGAINST WHAT. _VETOES_HAVE_DIFFERENT_HALF_LIVES.status: DURABLE governance rule for re-grading a previously declined candidate. Not session-scoped; do not delete at the bell. Read with _CONFIRMED_TRIGGERS_HAVE_A_SHELF_LIFE (the same staleness idea aimed at triggers rather than vetoes).
_VETOES_HAVE_DIFFERENT_HALF_LIVES.claim: A DECLINE IS USUALLY OVERDETERMINED, AND ITS REASONS DECAY AT DIFFERENT RATES. A TAPE veto (trend-maturity clause (c) -- 'the present tape does not confirm') goes stale within an hour. A STRUCTURAL veto (a flat-to-falling 200-day, distance off the 52-week high, sector concentration against an existing position) does not decay at all on an intraday horizon. Re-testing the expiring veto is correct and cheap; the failure is re-testing it IN ISOLATION and reading its expiry as a green light. BEFORE re-testing an expiring veto, re-read the original decline and establish whether that veto was ever the BINDING one.

_ENTRY_DAY_BAR_IS_NOT_THE_POSITIONS_BAR.status: DURABLE measurement rule for any P/L, excursion or holding-period statistic computed from daily bars. Not session-scoped. Same family as the affordability-tier and denominator bugs: a number taken from a convenient source that was never the thing being asked about.
_ENTRY_DAY_BAR_IS_NOT_THE_POSITIONS_BAR.claim: ON THE ENTRY DAY, THE DAILY BAR'S HIGH AND LOW BOUND THE STOCK, NOT THE TRADE. The position exists for only part of that session, so an entry-day extreme may have occurred before the fill. The error is DIRECTIONAL for mean-reversion entries: an RSI2 buy fills near the day's LOW after a decline, so the pre-entry HIGH is systematically flattering to the trade's measured excursion.
_ENTRY_DAY_BAR_IS_NOT_THE_POSITIONS_BAR.measured: Auditing the desk's own five swing entries. First pass included each entry day's full range and returned PNC max favorable excursion +3.43%, 'best excursion covered 93.7% of the distance to target' -- a reading that supports the conclusion that the trade nearly worked and gave it back. PNC's ledger entry is 246.4729 against an 08-19 daily CLOSE of 246.46, a 0.005% difference, so the fill was AT the close; that session opened 254.49 and fell all day, putting the 254.93 high entirely before the position existed. Corrected from the first bar that could contain the fill: MFE +0.56% (08-20 high 247.86), progress to target 15.4%. A 6x error on the excursion and more than 6x on the progress figure.
_ENTRY_DAY_BAR_IS_NOT_THE_POSITIONS_BAR.the_detector: Before using any entry-day extreme, compare the fill price to that day's OPEN and CLOSE. A fill at or near the close means the whole day's range is pre-entry -- discard it and measure from the next session. Where the fill TIME is known the entry-day range is legitimately usable: MDLZ 13:40:03Z, ROST 13:37:13Z and MMM 13:37:54Z all filled within minutes of the open, so their entry-day highs are real. get_equity_orders returns the fill timestamp; use it rather than inferring.
_ENTRY_DAY_BAR_IS_NOT_THE_POSITIONS_BAR.why_it_matters_beyond_one_row: It is the first instance of this failure family aimed at the desk's OWN P/L rather than at a market input -- which is exactly where it is least likely to be double-checked, because a flattering number about your own trade does not look like a data error. Any future hit-rate, MFE/MAE, or Friday review statistic computed from daily bars inherits this bug unless the fill timing is checked.
_ENTRY_DAY_BAR_IS_NOT_THE_POSITIONS_BAR.honest_scope: Caught inside the audit before anything was concluded from it, so no decision was made on the wrong number and no trade was licensed or blocked. Recorded because the wrong figure would have passed review: it was arithmetically correct, internally consistent, and pointed the opposite way.

_COHORT_SHRINKAGE_IS_SELECTION_ON_THE_OU.I_CAUGHT_MY_OWN_DENOMINATOR_BUG_IN_THE_H: The first framing of the retest was a RATIO -- 3.23x -> 4.68x the index decline -- which reads as catastrophic deterioration. It is inflated by a SHRINKING DENOMINATOR: SPY's own decline narrowed from -0.4497% to -0.3392%, so the ratio would have risen even had the cohort not moved at all. This is the fifth instance of this file's denominator family (session-average too strict, trailing-local too easy in a decaying tape, closing-auction too easy, the 5-min/1-min substitution direction) and the FIRST caught inside the desk's own headline number rather than in a market input. REPORT THE SPREAD IN POINTS, NEVER THE RATIO, when both legs of a relative measure are moving. The conclusion survives on the spread (-1.0027 -> -1.2472 pts) but the ratio overstated the deterioration roughly threefold.
_COHORT_SHRINKAGE_IS_SELECTION_ON_THE_OU.population_caveat_stated_because_it_limi: The 15:27Z measurement covered 15 non-held candidates; today's matched set is 17. They are not identical populations -- names entered and left the screen between the two readings -- so the comparison is indicative, not exact. It is quoted on the matched basis precisely so the direction is not an artifact of including the desk's own five holdings, which are the BEST subgroup on the day (-0.8225% vs the cohort's -1.4129%).
_COHORT_SHRINKAGE_IS_SELECTION_ON_THE_OU.the_transferable_lesson: When a screen's MEMBERSHIP is a function of the variable you are trying to measure, membership changes carry no information about that variable. Measure the FIXED set across time, not the set as currently constituted. Same family as the survivorship and denominator findings: a statistic that is cheap, intuitive, and defined in terms of its own outcome.

_RSI2_REVERSION_AND_PROFIT_NEED_NOT_COIN.the_transferable_mechanism: RSI2 is a RELATIVE oscillator normalized to recent range, so it re-baselines to wherever price has settled.
