This asks what happens the first time they do. Minted as a sub-object rather than a new top-level key per the CLAUDE.md rule that a contribution narrowing an existing subject edits that key.
THE_SUCCESSOR_QUESTION_THE_GATE_HAS_A_SI.the_live_case: MDLZ at 13:46Z: 62.625 vs entry 62.5899 = +0.056% -- GREEN, the first position in the book's life to be green with a rising RSI2 -- and own-computed RSI2 66.2 against the 70 trigger. Both legs of the mechanical profit-banking authority are within reach on the SAME name on the SAME day for the first time. It has NOT fired: 66.2 < 70, so nothing is due this run.
THE_SUCCESSOR_QUESTION_THE_GATE_HAS_A_SI.the_arithmetic_precomputed_so_no_future_: 7.988509 sh, cost basis $500.00. At 62.625 the position is worth $500.28 = +$0.28. Market 62.63 x 62.66, mid 62.645, spread 0.03 = 0.048% of mid -- unusually tight, and the bid sits ABOVE the last trade, so a sale at the bid nets about +$0.32. Either way the mechanical exit would bank roughly THIRTY CENTS on a $500 position, and would surrender a full position slot plus $500 of capital at a moment when deployable cash is only $302.10 and the rotation rule requires any replacement idea to beat the weakest name already held.
THE_SUCCESSOR_QUESTION_THE_GATE_HAS_A_SI.THE_FINDING: The 2026-08-26 correction gave this gate a SIGN -- it may only bank a profit, never realize a loss on a technical bounce -- and it did not give it a MAGNITUDE. Read literally, 'price > entry' is a boolean satisfied at +0.06% just as at +6%. A gate with no minimum will eventually fire a round trip whose gain is smaller than its own frictions.
THE_SUCCESSOR_QUESTION_THE_GATE_HAS_A_SI.the_governing_reading_for_the_run_that_f: HARD RULE 5 settles this and the prompt's compressed one-liner does not: the rule says 'Take profits when it makes SENSE' and calls the trigger a TAKE-PROFIT. Banking $0.30 is not taking a profit. Per the governance clause -- where the prompt's summary is BROADER than the rule it summarises, the RULE governs -- an RSI2>=70 print on a position green by an economically trivial amount is a JUDGEMENT call, not a mechanical fire. Require the gain to be real relative to the round-trip cost and to the value of the position slot; otherwise hold and let the thesis or the target do the work.
THE_SUCCESSOR_QUESTION_THE_GATE_HAS_A_SI.the_shape_this_is_an_instance_of: This file's most-repeated pattern: a newly-granted authority arrives with its wording compressed, and the first run to face the trigger is the one most likely to read the compression literally. That is exactly how the same authority misfired on PNC at RSI2 78.5 while 0.34% underwater on 2026-08-26. The sign was fixed then; the magnitude is being fixed now, BEFORE it fires rather than after.
THE_SUCCESSOR_QUESTION_THE_GATE_HAS_A_SI.watchpoint_for_later_runs_today: MDLZ RSI2 66.2 and rising on a +0.89% session. If it crosses 70 while the position is green by a fraction of a percent, DO NOT fire mechanically -- apply the reading above, log the decision, and say plainly that the trigger was reached and declined on magnitude.

_OPENING_WINDOW_SLIPPAGE_ON_AUTONOMOUS_E.headline: EVERY AUTONOMOUS EQUITY ENTRY THIS BOOK HAS EVER PLACED WAS FILLED 6-10 MINUTES AFTER THE BELL, AND IN ALL FOUR CASES A MATERIALLY BETTER PRICE WAS AVAILABLE WITHIN THE NEXT 30 MINUTES -- MEAN 0.700%. THE RUN IS BUYING THE OPENING BOUNCE OF THE VERY DIP ITS SIGNAL TOLD IT TO BUY.

measurement.method: Fill price vs (a) its percentile of that session's eventual regular-hours range, (b) the best price actually printed in the 30 minutes AFTER the fill, (c) the session close.

GD._note: Session still open at measurement; range is 13:30-13:47Z only, so its percentile can still move. The 30-minute improvement figure is already realised.

measurement.aggregate: Mean fill percentile 73.6% of the session range; 3 of 4 landed in the top ~16%. Mean improvement available within 30 minutes 0.700% = ~$3.50 on a $500 entry, ~$14.00 across the four entries to date.
measurement.GD_detail: GD ran 371.51 (13:30 low) -> 375.305 (13:32-33 high) -> 370.415 (13:47 low). The 13:36:10Z fill at 374.4437 caught 82% of that opening pop and the whole move round-tripped inside eleven minutes. The fill also printed ABOVE the reported high (374.060) of the one-minute bar containing it, on a bar showing only 255 shares -- either a thin consolidated bar or a marketable order crossing a wide spread on a $374 name. GD currently quotes 0.153% of mid wide, so a market order there is not free.

_OPENING_WINDOW_SLIPPAGE_ON_AUTONOMOUS_E.THE_MECHANISM_and_it_is_the_transferable: The signal and the execution are fighting each other. The autonomous entry is sourced from an RSI2 MEAN-REVERSION screen computed on the PREVIOUS SESSION'S CLOSE (see _REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN: the fresh report does not land on master until ~14:15Z, so the first-post-open run always acts on yesterday's report). The opening ten minutes is precisely when yesterday's oversold names get their reflexive bounce. So the run reads 'this name is oversold as of last night' and then executes into the exact window where that oversold condition is being relieved. It buys the bounce it meant to buy the dip of.
_OPENING_WINDOW_SLIPPAGE_ON_AUTONOMOUS_E.WHY_NOBODY_CAUGHT_IT: This file already carries the rule 'NEVER price a decision off the opening auction print -- re-quote at least ~5 minutes after 13:30Z', and runs have obeyed it. But that rule was written about MARKS and DECISIONS (the 2026-08-21 QQQ 680P incident, where an opening print flipped the SIGN of a P/L reported to Ryan). Nobody applied it to EXECUTION. Re-quoting before deciding and then filling into the same window satisfies the letter of the rule and gets the artifact anyway -- this file's most-repeated defect, a check that passes for the wrong reason. It is also the execution-layer sibling of the documented first-hour volume inflation: the opening bar carried 5.2x the next bar's volume on ROST and 2.3x on MDLZ, which is the same auction imbalance seen from the fill side instead of the denominator side.
_OPENING_WINDOW_SLIPPAGE_ON_AUTONOMOUS_E.THE_FIX_and_it_repairs_TWO_findings_with: PREFER to take the trading day's autonomous equity entry on the first run at or after ~14:15Z, once the fresh report has landed on master, rather than on the first-post-open run. Nothing in the thesis decays in 40 minutes: the hold is 1-3 weeks and the signal is already a day old. The same deferral ALSO retires _REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN's standing problem, because the run would then be acting on the CURRENT session's report instead of the prior one. Two known defects, one change, no gate loosened.
_OPENING_WINDOW_SLIPPAGE_ON_AUTONOMOUS_E.SCOPE_AND_LIMITS_stated_because_overclai: n=4 and the total measured cost is ~$14. This is a process refinement, NOT a crisis, and it must not be written up as one. Three caveats: (1) buying lower is not automatically better for a mean-reversion entry -- if a name keeps falling the later fill wins, if it reverts immediately the earlier fill wins; what is notable is that the improvement was available in 4 of 4 cases, not that it is guaranteed. (2) ROST filled at 44.3% of its range, so 'the run always buys the top' would be false. (3) GD's session is incomplete. The deferral is a PREFERENCE, not a bar: a genuinely time-critical signal still trades when it fires, and the entry must never be delayed past the point where the setup is gone.
_OPENING_WINDOW_SLIPPAGE_ON_AUTONOMOUS_E.what_it_does_NOT_change: No gate is loosened or tightened by this. The full HARD RULE 6 stack -- HARD RULE 7 thesis check, A-grade-only bar, capital policy, sector steer, [ERN] rule, per-name and spec caps, HARD RULE 3 market-order mechanics, HARD RULE 5's no-stops policy, 1/run and 3/day throttles -- applies unchanged. This is about WHEN in the session a cleared entry is executed, never about WHETHER it clears.

_OPENING_WINDOW_DECAY_HITS_THE_EVIDENCE_.headline: THE 2026-08-21 OPENING-WINDOW RE-QUOTE RULE WAS APPLIED TO THE PRICE BEING PAID AND NOT TO THE TAPE EVIDENCE THAT JUSTIFIED PAYING IT. THE EVIDENCE LEG DECAYED 65-72% IN THIRTEEN MINUTES ON A FLAT SPY.
_OPENING_WINDOW_DECAY_HITS_THE_EVIDENCE_.what_the_13_36Z_run_did_right_first: It followed the 2026-08-21T13:32Z rule exactly: it refused to price the GD order off the 13:31/13:32Z opening prints and re-quoted via review_equity_order at 13:35:40Z. Its own brief says so. The PRICE leg was protected. This finding is not a criticism of that -- it is the half the rule does not cover.
_OPENING_WINDOW_DECAY_HITS_THE_EVIDENCE_.the_gap: The entry's decisive evidence was a RELATIVE-STRENGTH reading taken in the same opening window: 'ITA +0.534% against SPY -0.678%, with ALL SIX primes green -- an advance, not merely an absence of decline', which is what refuted the prior session's case-(c) veto. That reading is a tape measurement made four minutes after the bell, and nothing in this file had ever applied the opening-window caution to a measurement used as EVIDENCE rather than as a PRICE.
_OPENING_WINDOW_DECAY_HITS_THE_EVIDENCE_.method: Minute closes from get_equity_historicals(interval='minute'), interpolated bars (GD 13:44; ITA 13:32/13:37/13:46) excluded. Prior-session closes from get_equity_quotes: GD 371.35, ITA 228.35, SPY 767.05. Relative strength = name's day-change minus SPY's day-change, in percentage points.

the_decay_table_pp_vs_SPY.13:34Z: GD +1.462pp | ITA +1.166pp  <- the window the 13:36Z run measured in

_OPENING_WINDOW_DECAY_HITS_THE_EVIDENCE_.magnitude: GD's relative strength fell 72% from the 13:33Z peak and 65% from the fill minute; ITA's fell 68%. SPY was FLAT across the entire window (761.812 -> 761.940, +0.017%), so this is decay in the names, not a move in the denominator. In ABSOLUTE terms the cited fact has inverted: GD went +1.065% -> -0.183% on the day and ITA +0.504% -> -0.289%, so 'all six primes green' and 'an advance' no longer describe the tape thirteen minutes after they were written.
_OPENING_WINDOW_DECAY_HITS_THE_EVIDENCE_.feed_integrity_checked_first: Per the 2026-08-28 direction rule. GD 5-minute buckets equal their 1-minute sums EXACTLY (2950/2950, 2486/2486, 2117/2117); ITA 4994/4994 exact; SPY 587,021 vs a 579,925 1-minute sum = +1.22%, inside tolerance and in the benign direction. No hole propagated into any number above.
_OPENING_WINDOW_DECAY_HITS_THE_EVIDENCE_.the_transferable_mechanism: An opening-window reading is an UPPER BOUND on whatever it measures, and this file already knows that for ATM IV (four confirmations, -2.5% to -4.4%) and for a position mark (the 2026-08-21 QQQ incident, where the SIGN of the P/L was wrong). The common cause is that the first minutes carry auction residue and thin two-sided flow, and that is a property of the TAPE, not of the quantity being read off it. So it applies identically to a relative-strength reading, a breadth count, or a 'whole complex is green' claim. THE RULE: any opening-window number that GATES a decision -- not merely the number being paid -- must be re-measured after ~14:00Z before it is treated as established, or must be carried forward explicitly labelled as provisional.
_OPENING_WINDOW_DECAY_HITS_THE_EVIDENCE_.why_it_is_worse_for_a_thin_name_than_for: GD traded 2,950 / 2,486 / 2,117 shares in the three opening 5-minute buckets against SPY's 587,021 / 314,097 / 205,181. A relative-strength ratio whose numerator is that thin has a materially shorter half-life than one built on an index, so the re-measure duty binds HARDEST exactly where the desk's equity candidates live -- mid-cap single names out of the RSI2 screen, not the core IV list.
_OPENING_WINDOW_DECAY_HITS_THE_EVIDENCE_.HONEST_SCOPE_this_changed_no_decision_an: GD is HELD and stays held. No mechanical exit fires (target 387.04 untouched; RSI2 13.8, nowhere near 70; the position is -0.72%, so the profit-banking authority is unavailable by construction under the 2026-08-26 gate). HARD RULE 5 forbids a price stop and permits an equity sale only on a target hit, an RSI2>=70 print while green, or a HARD RULE 7 THESIS break -- and a thirteen-minute tape decay is not a thesis break. The STRUCTURAL legs of the GD case are untouched by this measurement: the 08-31 seven-year DoD framework, the FactSet mean PT 424.50 / Overweight, the verified earnings-clear window, and RSI2 6.8 depth at entry all still stand. Only the TAPE leg decayed. Recorded per this file's standard that a measurement is creditable precisely because the audit does not license the action it might seem to argue for.
_OPENING_WINDOW_DECAY_HITS_THE_EVIDENCE_.HONEST_SCOPE_limits_of_the_measurement: Thirteen minutes is a very short window and intraday relative strength oscillates -- this may fully revert by the close, and n=1 on one entry is not evidence about the screen. The claim is narrow and is about MEASUREMENT TIMING, not about whether GD was a good buy. A later run should re-measure the same three series after 14:00Z rather than inheriting either the 13:34Z reading or this one.
_OPENING_WINDOW_DECAY_HITS_THE_EVIDENCE_.what_a_future_run_should_do_differently: When an entry gate turns on a tape comparison and the run fires inside the opening window, either (a) wait for the ~14:00Z re-measure before treating the comparison as established, or (b) take the entry and write the comparison down as PROVISIONAL with the re-measure scheduled -- never hand it forward as a settled fact, which is how the 2026-08-28 regime-label finding says a stale verdict propagates through the relay.

_UNION_MERGE_DEDUP_KEY_SILENTLY_DROPS_EN.headline: THE UNION-MERGE RULE SAYS 'KEEP BOTH JOURNAL ENTRIES' BUT NEVER SAYS HOW TO IDENTIFY A DUPLICATE, AND THE OBVIOUS KEY -- (run_utc, headline-prefix) -- SILENTLY DELETES REAL HISTORY. CAUGHT BY AN ARITHMETIC ASSERTION, NOT BY READING THE FILE.
_UNION_MERGE_DEDUP_KEY_SILENTLY_DROPS_EN.evidence: Resolving the 2026-09-01 13:52Z/13:55Z collision, a first attempt deduped on (run_utc, headline[:60]) and produced 784 entries from two 787-entry sides. The correct union is 788 (786 common + one entry per run). FOUR pre-existing entry PAIRS -- 2026-08-13T18:30Z, 2026-08-13T23:29Z, 2026-08-14T17:15Z, 2026-08-14T19:15Z -- legitimately share both run_utc and headline prefix, themselves the surviving records of earlier collisions. The dedup treated each pair as one entry and dropped its twin.
_UNION_MERGE_DEDUP_KEY_SILENTLY_DROPS_EN.the_rule: Dedup journal entries on FULL-CONTENT identity (json.dumps(entry, sort_keys=True)), never on a summary key. Two entries that differ anywhere are two entries. Then ASSERT the count: len(merged) == len(ours) + len(theirs) - len(common). Three lines of arithmetic catch this; reading the file does not, which is exactly why it nearly shipped.
_UNION_MERGE_DEDUP_KEY_SILENTLY_DROPS_EN.why_it_is_the_dangerous_direction: The failure is SILENT and IRREVERSIBLE in the direction that matters -- a merge that drops history produces a perfectly valid JSON file, a plausible entry count, and a clean git diff. Nothing errors. This is the same shape as the lot-invariant rule ('assert, don't read') and the `git diff --stat` rule: trust the check, not your sense of having been careful.
_UNION_MERGE_DEDUP_KEY_SILENTLY_DROPS_EN.scope: Caught before the push, so nothing was lost. Recorded because the collision protocol is exercised rarely and under time pressure, and the next run to hit one will reach for the same obvious key.

_IV_DAY_OVER_DAY_DIFFS_NEED_A_TIME_OFFSE.headline: A DAY-OVER-DAY ATM-IV DIFF IS ONLY MEANINGFUL IF THE TWO READINGS WERE TAKEN AT THE SAME TIME OF DAY, AND THIS FILE'S ROWS MOSTLY DO NOT RECORD WHEN THEY WERE TAKEN. TODAY'S SWEEP IS ~14 MINUTES LATER THAN YESTERDAY'S, WHICH BIASES EVERY DIFF DOWNWARD BY ROUGHLY THE SIZE OF THE EFFECT BEING MEASURED.
_IV_DAY_OVER_DAY_DIFFS_NEED_A_TIME_OFFSE.the_measurement: The 2026-08-31 core-list sweep was quoted 13:49:44Z; this run's is 14:03:13Z. The 08-31 rows already carry a _cross_validation finding that two honest reads of the SAME contracts minutes apart disagreed by +1.5% to +1.9% (TSM -0.34%), so a later read carries a systematic downward artifact budget of about that size against an earlier one. Raw day-over-day atm_iv: SPY +3.73%, QQQ +1.20%, NVDA -2.01%, AMD -6.97%, TSM -2.99%, AVGO -0.91%, MSFT -3.08%, TSLA -1.43%.
_IV_DAY_OVER_DAY_DIFFS_NEED_A_TIME_OFFSE.what_survives_the_correction: TWO READINGS, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, AND EVERYTHING ELSE IS UNMEASURED RATHER THAN FLAT. SPY +3.73% and QQQ +1.20% rose DESPITE an artifact that should have pushed them down, so index implied vol genuinely firmed on a -0.61% / -1.25% risk-off session and is if anything understated here. AMD -6.97% fell roughly 5.5% more than the artifact can explain, on a session where AMD itself fell -2.65% -- vol declining into a sharp price drop, which is the opposite of fear pricing. NVDA, TSM, AVGO, MSFT and TSLA are all inside or barely outside the budget and carry LITTLE OR NO SIGNAL; reporting them as 'single-name vol fell across the board' would have been a clean, wrong, six-for-six story.
_IV_DAY_OVER_DAY_DIFFS_NEED_A_TIME_OFFSE.the_near_miss: THIS RUN NEARLY WROTE THAT STORY. Six of six single names printed lower and two of two index ETFs printed higher -- a textbook dispersion signature, internally consistent, and exactly the kind of confluence the 2026-08-28 mid-event finding warns reads as conviction when it is really one artifact applied uniformly. The tell was that the artifact and the 'signal' point the same way for six of the eight names, which is what a shared measurement offset looks like from the inside.
_IV_DAY_OVER_DAY_DIFFS_NEED_A_TIME_OFFSE.the_durable_fix: EVERY IV ROW FROM HERE CARRIES measured_utc, and no run quotes a day-over-day diff without stating the time offset between the two readings. Most existing rows lack the field entirely -- today's offset had to be reconstructed from prose caveats buried in the 08-31 rows, which is why this went unnoticed for at least two sweeps. The eight rows written this run all carry it.
_IV_DAY_OVER_DAY_DIFFS_NEED_A_TIME_OFFSE.the_counter_hypothesis_explicitly_reject: 'Tight chains reproduce, wide chains do not' is NOT supported and must not be adopted as a shortcut. On 08-31 the WIDEST chain on the sweep (TSM, 14.4% of mid) had the SMALLEST disagreement (-0.34%) while the TIGHTEST (TSLA, 1.4%) disagreed by +1.53%. At n=5 the relationship is absent or inverted. Reproducibility is established by measuring it, never inferred from chain width -- otherwise the desk grants itself permission to trust exactly the readings it has not checked.
_IV_DAY_OVER_DAY_DIFFS_NEED_A_TIME_OFFSE.honest_scope: IT CHANGED NO DECISION. Both options tracks were declined on capital ($302.10 deployable) and regime (an unresolved two-night earnings cluster) before any of these numbers could gate anything, and AMD's surviving vol decline is a watch item and emphatically not a candidate -- cheap, liquid vol supplies no thesis, and AMD's put chain at 14.31% of mid is the sweep's worst. Recorded per this desk's standard that a measurement audit is creditable precisely when it does not license the action it might seem to argue for. n=1 offset comparison on one pair of sweeps; the artifact budget itself rests on the 08-31 n=5 cross-validation and is an estimate, not a constant.
_IV_DAY_OVER_DAY_DIFFS_NEED_A_TIME_OFFSE.also_recorded_the_settled_remeasure: The three rows the 13:51Z run wrote inside the opening window were re-measured 12 minutes later and moved only -0.18% (SPY), -0.25% (QQQ) and -0.73% (NVDA) -- an order of magnitude smaller than the -2.53%/-4.37%/-3.56% settles recorded 2026-08-27. That is NOT the caveat being wrong: those settles compared ~13:41Z rows against ~14:47Z ones, and the 13:51Z rows had already had 21 minutes to settle, so this is a weaker test of the residual only. It bounds rather than discharges. Full text in iv_history.json under each row's _settled_remeasure.

_SETUP_INVALIDATION_MISSING_ON_MOST_OF_T.headline: FOUR OF SIX EQUITY POSITIONS CARRIED NO setup_invalidation FIELD -- INCLUDING ONE OPENED 44 MINUTES EARLIER -- WHILE PROMPT v8 STATES 'No written invalidation = no trade'. SWEPT AND FILLED THIS RUN.
_SETUP_INVALIDATION_MISSING_ON_MOST_OF_T.what_was_missing: PNC (entered 2026-08-19), MDLZ (08-28), MMM (08-31) and GD (09-01, 13:36:10Z) all lacked the field. Only LLY and ROST had it. The book has been running four positions on an absent exit plan -- for PNC, thirteen calendar days.
_SETUP_INVALIDATION_MISSING_ON_MOST_OF_T.why_it_survived_and_it_is_this_file's_mo: The defect was ALREADY FOUND AND ALREADY NAMED. On 2026-08-28T13:58Z a third run added the field to ROST and wrote, in the field itself, 'the entry note recorded the report's advisory 220.01 but positions[] carried NO setup_invalidation field'. That run identified the class correctly and fixed exactly the one name in front of it. Nothing swept the rest, so three further entries were opened afterward without the field and the count went UP after the discovery, not down. A per-instance fix to a class defect leaves a written record that LOOKS like the class was handled.
_SETUP_INVALIDATION_MISSING_ON_MOST_OF_T.the_sub_case_that_makes_a_field_audit_ne: MDLZ is the instructive one: it already had a complete, well-reasoned invalidation -- 'a cut to the FY26 guidance just raised... or a close through the rising 200-day MA at 58.94' -- sitting in its _note PROSE. A human reading the ledger sees a position with a plan. A run reading positions[] programmatically sees nothing. Both readings are honest and they disagree, so 'I read the ledger and the positions look managed' is a check that passes for the wrong reason. The prose was promoted into the field verbatim this run.
_SETUP_INVALIDATION_MISSING_ON_MOST_OF_T.the_detector_assert_do_not_read: Before ending any run, assert it: `[p['symbol'] for p in holdings['positions'] if p.get('sleeve')!='options' and not p.get('setup_invalidation')]` must be EMPTY. One line, catches every future instance including ones opened by a sibling run minutes earlier. Same family as the git-diff --stat rule and the lot-count invariants: trust the assertion, never the enumeration or the impression.
_SETUP_INVALIDATION_MISSING_ON_MOST_OF_T.what_the_levels_are_and_are_NOT: Every level written is a THESIS-REVIEW TRIGGER, never an order. HARD RULE 5 stands unchanged: the agent places NO stop of any kind, and an underwater name with an intact thesis is held, not stopped out. The 200-day SMAs were computed THIS RUN from completed daily bars through 2026-08-31 and each verified RISING over the trailing 7 bars: PNC 223.51 (+2.0704), MDLZ 59.00 (+0.2326), MMM 160.88 (+0.4511), GD 354.14 (+1.2029).
_SETUP_INVALIDATION_MISSING_ON_MOST_OF_T.method_cross_check_so_the_sweep_is_not_a: MMM's entry run recorded a 200-day of 160.8617 on 2026-08-31; this run computed 160.8774 independently -- agreement to 1.6 cents. MDLZ's entry note recorded 58.94 four sessions before this run's 59.00, a 6-cent drift consistent with a rising average. Both confirm the levels being written now are the same measurement the entries themselves cleared.

_ABSENCE_FROM_THE_SIGNAL_TABLE_IS_NOT_SI.headline: GD SATISFIES THE COMMITTED REPORT'S OWN STATED RSI2<10 CRITERION AT THE REPORT'S OWN PRICE AND IS STILL ABSENT FROM ITS RSI2 TABLE. A NAME VANISHING FROM A SIGNAL LIST IS NOT EVIDENCE THE SIGNAL EXPIRED.
_ABSENCE_FROM_THE_SIGNAL_TABLE_IS_NOT_SI.the_measurement: The 2026-09-01T14:02Z latest_morning.md lists 28 RSI2 setups sorted ascending, running from AEHR 0.1 to SPY 9.9 -- so the table is bounded by the 10.0 cutoff, NOT truncated by row count. GD is absent from it. Computed independently this run from completed daily bars through 2026-08-31 plus the report's OWN quoted GD price of 371.53: Wilder RSI2 = 6.4, simple-average RSI2 = 2.2. Either method places GD comfortably inside the table, near the top of it. The other two gates pass too: the 200-day SMA of 354.14 is RISING (+1.2029 over 7 bars) and spot sits +4.8% above it.
_ABSENCE_FROM_THE_SIGNAL_TABLE_IS_NOT_SI.the_computation_is_validated_not_asserte: The two RSI2 methods BRACKET the report's own published values for names that DID appear -- report MMM 1.8 against this run's Wilder 1.5 / simple 0.0, and report ROST 3.1 against Wilder/simple in the same family. So the independent computation agrees with the report's method to within the Wilder-vs-simple spread; GD's absence is not a methodology disagreement.
_ABSENCE_FROM_THE_SIGNAL_TABLE_IS_NOT_SI.ruled_out: Not held-name exclusion: MMM and ROST are both held and both appear, tagged HELD. Not row-count truncation: the list runs to the 10.0 boundary. Not the trend gate: rising 200-day, price above it. GD does appear in the report's PORTFOLIO REVIEW table (priced 371.53), so the report knows the name -- it is missing from the SIGNAL tables specifically.
_ABSENCE_FROM_THE_SIGNAL_TABLE_IS_NOT_SI.inferred_cause_stated_as_inference_not_f: Most likely a per-symbol data fetch failure in report.py's FMP screen, which this playbook already documents as degrading silently on API failure (the earnings calendar degrades to {} the same way). The portfolio table is built from the ledger plus a separate quote, which is why the name survives there and not in the screen. NOT PROVEN FROM THIS ENVIRONMENT -- report.py cannot be run here (no FMP reachability, network allowlist), so no run should upgrade this to a diagnosis without reproducing it.
_ABSENCE_FROM_THE_SIGNAL_TABLE_IS_NOT_SI.why_it_matters_and_it_is_the_exit_side_n: Prompt v8's equity book is SIGNAL-SOURCED ONLY. The obvious cost is a missed entry, and that is the small half. The dangerous half: a future run comparing today's report against a position bought yesterday can read the name's disappearance as 'the setup expired' and treat it as grounds to exit. It is not. Under HARD RULE 5 and HARD RULE 6 an exit needs a target hit, an RSI2>=70 print on a GREEN position, or a HARD RULE 7 thesis BREAK -- absence from a screen is none of those, and on this measurement it is not even evidence the technical condition ended.
_ABSENCE_FROM_THE_SIGNAL_TABLE_IS_NOT_SI.standing_instruction: Before drawing any conclusion from a name's absence from the report's signal tables, RECOMPUTE the criterion yourself from daily bars. Absence is a question, never an answer.

_THE_OPENING_DEFERRAL_HAS_NO_ENFORCEMENT.headline: THIS RUN IS THE EXACT RUN THE 13:50Z OPENING-WINDOW FIX WAS WRITTEN FOR -- FIRST RUN AT/AFTER ~14:15Z WITH THE CURRENT SESSION'S REPORT ON MASTER -- AND IT CANNOT ACT, BECAUSE THE DAY'S CAPITAL WAS SPENT 39 MINUTES BEFORE THE WINDOW OPENED.
_THE_OPENING_DEFERRAL_HAS_NO_ENFORCEMENT.the_sequence: GD filled 13:36:10Z off the STALE 2026-08-31T19:27Z report. The current session's report landed on master at 14:02Z, 26 minutes AFTER the fill. This run fires 14:15Z with the fresh report available and deployable capital of $302.10 -- below the ~$400 practical equity entry minimum. The entry throttle is NOT the binding constraint (1 of 3 used for the day, 0 of 1 this run); CAPITAL is.
_THE_OPENING_DEFERRAL_HAS_NO_ENFORCEMENT.the_structural_point: The 2026-09-01T13:50Z finding prescribes 'PREFER to take the trading day's autonomous equity entry on the first run at or after ~14:15Z'. It is a PREFERENCE held independently by each run, and nothing reserves the capital or the opportunity for the window. Any earlier run that judges its own signal good enough spends the money, and the window-run then inherits a position it would not have sized from today's screen and has nothing left to deploy. A deferral rule whose precondition (capital still available when the window opens) is unprotected is advisory in name and inoperative in practice.
_THE_OPENING_DEFERRAL_HAS_NO_ENFORCEMENT.do_not_overclaim_this: GD is ALREADY the fourth case in the 13:50Z finding's 4-of-4 slippage measurement (1.076%); this run adds NO new n to that count and must not be read as doing so. GD at 371.03 vs the 374.4437 fill is -0.91%, which is the same artifact already recorded, re-observed later in the session. What is new here is not slippage evidence -- it is the observation that the prescribed remedy is structurally unenforceable, which would be true even if every fill had been perfect.
_THE_OPENING_DEFERRAL_HAS_NO_ENFORCEMENT.what_this_does_NOT_license: It is NOT grounds to sell GD. The 13:36Z entry cleared its full gate stack, its thesis is intact and improving, and an execution-timing artifact is not a thesis event. It is also NOT grounds for a run to hoard capital against a later window -- CLAUDE.md's capital policy forbids an unexpiring hold and requires any deliberate cash hold to name a catalyst, a checkable trigger and an expiry.
_THE_OPENING_DEFERRAL_HAS_NO_ENFORCEMENT.the_honest_options_and_both_are_Ryan's_c: (a) Leave it advisory and accept that the earliest run of the day usually spends the entry -- cost is the measured ~0.7% mean slippage plus acting on a day-old screen. (b) Make it a duty in the routine prompt: no autonomous equity entry before the current session's report is on master, except a genuinely time-critical signal. Only (b) is enforceable, and only Ryan can make it, because a run DUTY changes only when he re-pastes the prompt -- agents cannot edit it. FLAGGED, NOT DECIDED.

BEFORE TREATING A GREEN NAME AS THE EXCEPTION, CHECK TWO THINGS THAT COST NOTHING: (1) is its greenness an artifact of a DIVIDEND ADJUSTMENT, and (2) is it green relative to its own SECTOR, or merely carried by it? _COHORT_EXCEPTION_NEEDS_A_DIVIDEND_AND_S.the_mechanism: A dividend adjustment shifts the denominator of the day-change calculation without any trade occurring. On a day when the whole cohort is red, a name going ex-dividend is the most likely name to appear green, because the adjustment credits it with the dividend it just paid away. So the cohort rule's exception clause is BIASED TOWARD SELECTING EX-DIVIDEND NAMES as the one worth working -- exactly the names where the greenness is least informative about whether buyers are present.
_COHORT_EXCEPTION_NEEDS_A_DIVIDEND_AND_S.the_detector: When the cohort produces exactly one green name, before working it: (a) compare adjusted_previous_close to previous_close on that name -- any gap is a corporate action, and the raw figure is the one that says whether it actually traded up; (b) quote its sector ETF at the same timestamp and require the name to beat it, not merely to be green while the sector is green. Both come free from calls the run already makes.
_COHORT_EXCEPTION_NEEDS_A_DIVIDEND_AND_S.honest_scope: IT CHANGED NO DECISION. The entry was declined on the cohort distribution (4.9x, 17 of 20 underperforming) before the exception was examined, and would have been declined had GS been genuinely green -- one session of relative strength does not repair a weak setup, as the parent finding already states. Recorded because a filter's inputs can only be audited credibly on a run where the audit does not license a trade. n=1 green name on n=1 session; the MECHANISM is general, the magnitude is not.
_COHORT_EXCEPTION_NEEDS_A_DIVIDEND_AND_S.family: Same class as the affordability-tier bug (spot price / ATM strike / wrong expiry board), the four denominator modes, and the entry-day-bar error: a number taken from a convenient field that was never quite the thing being asked about. This is its first appearance in the EQUITY cohort screen rather than in an options or volume input.

_UNION_MERGE_WEDGES_THE_PR_HEAD_ON_GITHU.status: DURABLE repo-mechanics note. Not session-scoped; not a trading rule. Read it when a union merge will not land.
_UNION_MERGE_WEDGES_THE_PR_HEAD_ON_GITHU.claim: AFTER RESOLVING A CONCURRENT-RUN UNION MERGE AND PUSHING, GITHUB MAY KEEP THE PR PINNED TO ITS PRE-MERGE HEAD SHA AND REPORT `mergeable_state: dirty` FOREVER. The branch is fine; the PR object is stale. Do not re-resolve the conflict -- there is nothing left to resolve.
_UNION_MERGE_WEDGES_THE_PR_HEAD_ON_GITHU.observed: PR #949. Local and remote branch both at the union-merge commit 4557819, `git log HEAD..origin/master` EMPTY (strictly ahead, no conflict), yet the PR read head.sha 826f945 / commits:1 / mergeable_state 'dirty' across three merge attempts and two re-reads several minutes apart. `update_pull_request_branch` returned 'expected head sha didn't match current head ref', which CONFIRMS the staleness rather than fixing it. A second PR cannot be opened from the same branch (GitHub 422).
_UNION_MERGE_WEDGES_THE_PR_HEAD_ON_GITHU.the_fix: Close the PR and immediately reopen it, then merge. That forces GitHub to recompute the head and mergeability; #949 merged on the next attempt.
_UNION_MERGE_WEDGES_THE_PR_HEAD_ON_GITHU.the_caveat_state_it_when_you_use_it: The drive-to-green rules name 'close and reopen the PR to kick CI' as a NEVER. This is NOT that, and the distinction must be stated whenever the technique is used: nothing was red, this repo runs no CI on ledger PRs, and the purpose was to refresh a wedged mergeability computation so an already-resolved merge could land -- not to re-roll a failing check. If a PR here is ever genuinely red, close/reopen is forbidden and stays forbidden.
_UNION_MERGE_WEDGES_THE_PR_HEAD_ON_GITHU.cheaper_first_moves: Before reaching for it: (1) re-read the PR -- GitHub's mergeability is async and often settles on its own; (2) confirm with `git log HEAD..origin/master` that the branch really is conflict-free, so you are not papering over a real conflict. Only when the PR stays pinned to a superseded SHA is this a wedge rather than a genuine conflict.
_UNION_MERGE_WEDGES_THE_PR_HEAD_ON_GITHU.why_it_will_recur: Concurrent same-slot runs are an intermittent but ongoing condition (documented 2026-08-13, 2026-08-28, 2026-08-31, 2026-09-01), and EVERY collision produces a union merge -- so every collision is a chance to hit this. The trigger config is Ryan's to change; an agent can only make each collision cheap to clear.

_MECHANICAL_EXIT_HAS_NO_MAGNITUDE_FLOOR.headline: THE MECHANICAL TAKE-PROFIT'S TWO GATES ARE NEAR-INDEPENDENT, SO 'RSI2>=70 AND GREEN' CAN BOTH BE TRUE AT A GAIN OF A FEW CENTS. MEASURED ON MDLZ: THE AUTHORITY FIRES AT 62.7337 = +0.230% = $1.15 GROSS, AGAINST THE TRADE'S OWN $16.86 TARGET. THAT IS 6.8% OF THE OBJECTIVE, AND IT IS NOT A TAKE-PROFIT.
_MECHANICAL_EXIT_HAS_NO_MAGNITUDE_FLOOR.resolves: The open question raised by the 2026-09-01T13:55Z run ('an RSI2>=70 print on a trivially-green name banks cents while surrendering a slot') and explicitly left open by the 14:03Z run as 'stands recorded and undecided rather than resolved'. It is now measured and decided. A question handed forward twice without arithmetic is a question nobody has actually asked.
_MECHANICAL_EXIT_HAS_NO_MAGNITUDE_FLOOR.the_measurement: MDLZ, entry 62.5899 on 7.988509 sh ($500.00), target 64.70. Wilder RSI2 on completed daily closes through 2026-08-31 = 3.726 (deeply oversold). With the live 62.6219 appended: 66.07. Solved by bisection, RSI2 crosses 70 at 62.7337 -- only +0.230% above the entry. Gross gain at the trigger $1.15; gain at the target $16.86. So the mechanical authority, read literally, fires an exit worth 6.8% of the position's stated objective, on a name five sessions old, and consumes a book slot to do it.
_MECHANICAL_EXIT_HAS_NO_MAGNITUDE_FLOOR.the_mechanism_which_is_the_transferable_: RSI2 is a function of the RECENT PRICE PATH; P/L is a function of the ENTRY LEVEL. The two are near-independent, so the price at which the authority FIRES is set by one thing and the size of what it BANKS by another. A position entered at or near a local high -- which is exactly what a mean-reversion entry filled in the opening window tends to be, per _OPENING_WINDOW_SLIPPAGE_ON_AUTONOMOUS_EQUITY_ENTRIES -- satisfies both gates simultaneously at a trivial gain. The worse the entry, the smaller the gain at which the exit fires. The clause pays the desk least precisely where it executed worst.
_MECHANICAL_EXIT_HAS_NO_MAGNITUDE_FLOOR.this_is_the_MIRROR_of_the_hole_already_f: The 2026-08-26 correction added `price > entry` to stop the mechanical exit REALIZING A LOSS on a technical bounce (it fired on PNC at RSI2 78.5 while 0.34% underwater). That fix is correct and stands. But it only bounds the SIGN of the outcome, never its MAGNITUDE -- and nobody checked the other end, which is this file's most-repeated shape: a rule written to stop one failure mode is assumed to have bounded the whole quantity. Both holes live in the same sentence of HARD RULE 6, and neither is visible from the clause's wording.
_MECHANICAL_EXIT_HAS_NO_MAGNITUDE_FLOOR.the_rule: AN RSI2>=70 PRINT IS A MECHANICAL TAKE-PROFIT ONLY WHEN THE GAIN IS WORTH BANKING RELATIVE TO THE TRADE'S OWN WRITTEN TARGET. Concretely: require the banked gain to be at least roughly a THIRD of the entry-to-target distance. Below that the print is an OPTIONAL exit-into-strength carrying the same discretion as any other -- which under HARD RULE 5 means it needs a HARD RULE 7 thesis break or a graded ROTATION reason, never a technical trigger alone. This is the identical resolution the 2026-08-26 correction reached for the underwater case, applied to the trivially-green one, and it changes NO other gate: a target hit still banks, a real RSI2 bounce on a real gain still banks.
_MECHANICAL_EXIT_HAS_NO_MAGNITUDE_FLOOR.the_honest_counter_argument_because_it_i: Selling MDLZ at 62.73 would free ~$501 and take deployable capital from $302.10 to ~$803 -- enough to fund a fresh entry, which the book cannot do today. That is a REAL benefit and it must not be waved away. But it is a ROTATION argument, not a take-profit argument, and the rotation rule has its own requirement: the incoming idea must be GRADED and must beat the position being sold on the entry stack. No such graded candidate exists this run. Freeing capital for an idea you have not yet had is not rotation -- it is selling on the hope of a signal, which is the churn HARD RULE 5 forbids under a different name.
_MECHANICAL_EXIT_HAS_NO_MAGNITUDE_FLOOR.honest_scope: IT CHANGED NO DECISION ON THE RUN THAT FOUND IT: MDLZ printed 66.07, not 70, so the authority was never armed and nothing was declined that could have been taken. That is the only condition under which a filter's own thresholds can be audited credibly, and it is the same standard the volume-baseline findings in CLAUDE.md hold themselves to. n=1 name; the magnitude of the effect is a single-instance measurement, and the ~one-third fraction is a judgement, not a measured optimum. What IS established firmly is the STRUCTURAL point -- the two gates are near-independent, so no bound on the gain follows from either of them.
_MECHANICAL_EXIT_HAS_NO_MAGNITUDE_FLOOR.detector: Before treating an RSI2>=70 print as a mechanical fire, compute two numbers: the gain at the trigger price, and the gain at the position's written target. If the first is a small fraction of the second, the clause has fired on its technical leg while its economic leg is absent -- decline, and say which of the two it was. It is two lines of arithmetic and it uses the target already written in the ledger.
_MECHANICAL_EXIT_HAS_NO_MAGNITUDE_FLOOR._union_merge_note: UNION-MERGED 2026-09-01. Concurrent same-slot runs 14:30Z and 14:35Z both did genuine, non-overlapping work and both landed. Resolution per the CLAUDE.md rule (union, never pick a side): the 14:35Z run's _current_state_run and _last_reconciliation are kept because they are LATER, and this finding -- the 14:30Z run's sole unique contribution -- is preserved verbatim alongside them. Both journal entries are kept, ordered by run_utc. The two runs' independently-fetched reconciliations agree (1 option + 6 equities, zero drift), which is cross-validation rather than a conflict.

_ENTRY_PREMISE_WITHDRAWN_WITHIN_THE_SESS.headline: AN ENTRY JUSTIFIED BY A SAME-SESSION CROSS-SECTIONAL READING INHERITS THAT READING'S SHELF LIFE -- GD's 'whole defense complex is green' premise was measured in the opening six minutes and had FULLY INVERTED 70 minutes later, in the OPPOSITE direction to the tape.
_ENTRY_PREMISE_WITHDRAWN_WITHIN_THE_SESS.the_entry: 13:36:10Z, GD $500.00 -> 1.335314 sh @ 374.4437, placed_agent='agentic', order 6a96d4ca. Its stated justification, quoted from the heartbeat: 'a DELIBERATE, measured reversal of yesterday's GD veto: the whole defense complex went from -2.1% (4.4x SPY) on 08-31 to ALL SIX NAMES GREEN today against SPY -0.678%.'
_ENTRY_PREMISE_WITHDRAWN_WITHIN_THE_SESS.measured_now: At 14:46Z, FIVE OF SIX ARE RED and only HII is green -- GD -0.652% | LMT -0.899% (adjusted close; it is ex-dividend today) | NOC -0.500% | RTX -0.226% | LHX -1.140% | HII +0.100% | sector ETF ITA -0.819%. Meanwhile SPY IMPROVED from -0.678% to -0.392%. The complex went from outperforming a falling index while green, to underperforming a recovering one while red.
_ENTRY_PREMISE_WITHDRAWN_WITHIN_THE_SESS.the_finding: This is the 2026-08-31 concurrent-run lesson ('hand forward the NUMBERS, never the VERDICT') arriving one level up -- not on a regime LABEL but on an ENTRY THESIS. A cross-sectional breadth reading taken in the opening ten minutes is a timestamped observation with the same short shelf life as a regime label, and an entry that RESTS on one has bought the observation, not a thesis. The 08-31 veto and the 09-01 entry were decided by the same measurement taken on two different mornings; the measurement reversed twice inside 27 hours.
_ENTRY_PREMISE_WITHDRAWN_WITHIN_THE_SESS.what_it_does_NOT_license: IT IS NOT A SELL, and reading it as one would be the exact churn HARD RULE 5 forbids. GD is -1.47% ($-7.36) and underwater, so it carries NO price stop and is managed on thesis. There is no HARD RULE 7 thesis break: the move is SECTOR-WIDE (ITA -0.819%), and GD is OUTPERFORMING its own sector ETF by 17bp, which is the signature of complex beta rather than a name-specific break. Verdict: THESIS INTACT, HOLD.
_ENTRY_PREMISE_WITHDRAWN_WITHIN_THE_SESS.the_transferable_rule: When an entry's 'why NOW' is a same-session cross-sectional reading (breadth, complex-wide agreement, a cohort skew), say so explicitly in the entry note and treat the premise as EXPIRING AT THE BELL -- do not let a later run inherit it as though it were a durable thesis. A durable thesis survives its own session; a breadth reading is evidence about the next few hours. The 08-26 regime capstone is the same shape: participation that arrives at a level and then stops is real flow and still means nothing directionally.
_ENTRY_PREMISE_WITHDRAWN_WITHIN_THE_SESS.re_measured_2026-09-01T18-17Z: THIRD INVERSION OF THE SAME CROSS-SECTIONAL READING INSIDE ONE SESSION, AND IT FLIPPED BACK IN GD's FAVOUR -- which STRENGTHENS this key's rule rather than contradicting it. Sequence, all measured: (1) 13:34Z all six primes GREEN against SPY -0.678% (the premise that licensed the entry); (2) 14:46Z five of six RED and GD UNDERperforming a RECOVERING SPY by 26bp (the inversion recorded above); (3) 18:17Z the whole complex is red and now UNDERperforms a FALLING index -- ITA 225.805 -1.114%, NOC 533.71 -1.110%, LHX 263.395 -1.072%, RTX 205.585 -1.033%, LMT 545.3901 -2.221% (ex-dividend today, adjusted close 557.78), XLI 172.775 -1.345%, against SPY 761.395 -0.738% and QQQ 706.89 -1.377% -- BUT GD ITSELF IS THE STRONGEST NAME IN THE COMPLEX AT -0.399%, i.e. OUTperforming both SPY (+34bp) and its own sector ETF (+72bp). The relative reading has now reversed three times in 4h43m. WHAT IT CHANGES: NOTHING, and that is the point. GD is -1.22% vs entry on the 18:16Z quote 369.8675, underwater, so it carries no price stop and is managed on thesis; the move remains SECTOR-WIDE with GD the least-bad leg, which is complex beta and not a name-specific break. Verdict unchanged: THESIS INTACT, HOLD. THE EXTENSION TO THE RULE: a cross-sectional premise does not merely go stale, it OSCILLATES -- so a run that re-measures it and finds it favourable again must NOT read that as vindication of the entry, any more than the 14:46Z run read the adverse reading as a sell. Both directions are the same error. The premise expires at the bell in EITHER direction; only the thesis carries overnight.

_DIRECTION_RULE_SUBSTITUTION_IS_A_FLOOR.subject: A property of the 2026-08-28 feed-hole DIRECTION RULE itself, not another hole instance. The rule is correct; its prescribed substitution is systematically low.
_DIRECTION_RULE_SUBSTITUTION_IS_A_FLOOR.the_finding: When a 5-minute bucket reads materially BELOW its 1-minute sum, the direction rule says the bucket is holed and the sum substitutes. But the single defective minute that corrupted the bucket is ITSELF one of the five terms in that sum, so the substitution is a FLOOR, not a true value. Measured on the 2026-09-01 14:40Z bucket: SPY substituted 127,793 vs an imputed true ~143,626 (-11.0%); QQQ substituted 96,260 vs ~106,422 (-9.5%).
_DIRECTION_RULE_SUBSTITUTION_IS_A_FLOOR.evidence: SPY 14:40Z bucket reported 2,280 vs 1-min sum 127,793 (-98.2%); QQQ reported 4,436 vs 96,260 (-95.4%). Both reported volumes EQUAL their 14:44 one-minute bar exactly -- the single-constituent signature -- and SPY's bucket OHLC is byte-for-byte its 14:44 minute. The 14:44 minute is itself holed by this file's own recognition test (a tiny fraction of BOTH neighbours): SPY 2,280 = 12.9%/12.3% of neighbours, QQQ 4,436 = 30.8%/30.0%. CONTROL: IWM's 14:40Z bucket read 128,392 vs a 128,336 sum = +0.04%, CLEAN, in the same call.
_DIRECTION_RULE_SUBSTITUTION_IS_A_FLOOR.the_mechanism_transferable: The bucket does not merely under-report -- it ADOPTS the defective minute wholesale, OHLC included. The bad minute and the bad bucket are ONE defect seen at two resolutions, not two independent ones. That is why the direction rule works, and equally why it cannot be exact: you are summing a series containing the corruption you are correcting for.
_DIRECTION_RULE_SUBSTITUTION_IS_A_FLOOR.the_rule: Treat a direction-rule substitution as a FLOOR and label it one. When a bucket's reported volume EXACTLY equals one constituent minute, test that minute against its own neighbours before summing; if it also carries the hole signature, impute it at the neighbour mean and state a RANGE (floor = raw sum, estimate = sum with the bad minute imputed). On a borderline confirmation call use the IMPUTED figure -- it is conservative, because a larger denominator makes confirmation harder.
_DIRECTION_RULE_SUBSTITUTION_IS_A_FLOOR.direction_of_the_error: It understates a VOLUME DENOMINATOR, i.e. the confirmation-MANUFACTURING direction. This is now the fifth distinct way this file has recorded a denominator being wrong (session-average too strict; trailing-local too easy in a decaying tape; closing-auction too easy in absolute terms; holed bucket too low; and now the prescribed correction for that hole still ~10% too low).
_DIRECTION_RULE_SUBSTITUTION_IS_A_FLOOR.honest_scope: Changed no decision -- no trigger was tested and no volume baseline was load-bearing on the run that measured it. Both of that run's session-extreme claims survived the correction with room (SPY true bucket high 764.340 vs the 764.549 session high; QQQ 710.2297 vs 711.090). The imputation is an ESTIMATE from two neighbouring minutes, not a measurement: the 9.5-11% figure is indicative, n=2 symbols on one bucket.
_DIRECTION_RULE_SUBSTITUTION_IS_A_FLOOR._promoted_from: Absorbs the durable half of _QQQ_THIRD_HOLE_OF_SESSION_2026-08-28, which was session-scoped, marked 'delete at the next session's first post-bell cleanup', and had outlived its expiry by three sessions because deletion was nobody's job. Preserve the FINDING, retire the CONTAINER. Its two durable nuggets, kept verbatim in substance: (a) PRICE corruption observed live, not inferred -- that bucket's reported LOW understated the true 5-minute low by 0.25 points, the mechanism by which a hole corrupts LEVELS and not merely volume; (b) three holes in ~78 buckets on one symbol in one session is a ~3.8% per-symbol rate -- small sample, recorded so nobody treats holes as rare enough to skip the reconciliation.
_DIRECTION_RULE_SUBSTITUTION_IS_A_FLOOR.offset_hypothesis_stays_dead: Today's holes land at :40. Against 08-28's :05/:05/:20 and 08-27's :45, that is a fourth distinct offset. Hole offsets carry NO information -- reconcile every window you intend to use; never skip on a positional prior.

_A_ONE_DAY_MA_SLOPE_IS_NOT_A_FORWARD_PAT.headline: A ONE-DAY MOVING-AVERAGE SLOPE IS NOT A FORWARD PATH -- IT MEASURES THE SINGLE CLOSE THAT JUST ROLLED OUT, AND HERE IT OVERSTATED THE LEVEL'S FORWARD DRIFT BY 1.85x. ROLL THE WINDOW; DO NOT EXTRAPOLATE THE SLOPE.
_A_ONE_DAY_MA_SLOPE_IS_NOT_A_FORWARD_PAT.what_was_measured: QQQ's 50-day SMA at 16:30Z is 711.5868 against spot 708.450, i.e. the breakdown the 16:20Z run recorded is intact and has extended. The one-session-back slope is -0.4772/day, computed the obvious way (today's 50-day minus yesterday's). Linear extrapolation of that slope says the falling 50-day reaches spot in 711.5868-708.450 = 3.137 / 0.4772 = 6.6 sessions -- i.e. a MOTIONLESS QQQ is back above its 50-day inside seven sessions with no buying whatsoever, and the bearish break self-repairs.
_A_ONE_DAY_MA_SLOPE_IS_NOT_A_FORWARD_PAT.what_the_rolled_window_actually_says: WRONG, and by a lot. Rolling the 50-close window forward with QQQ pinned flat at 708.450 -- which is what the 2026-08-25 rule ('compute what LEAVES the window over the intended hold period') actually asks for -- gives the 50-day as 711.587 / 710.997 / 710.893 / 710.849 / 710.691 / 710.729 / 710.417 / 709.858 / 709.523 over sessions +0 through +8. That is a total decline of 2.064 points over eight sessions = -0.258/day, and it does NOT reach spot: eight sessions out, a motionless QQQ is still 1.07 points BELOW its 50-day. The naive slope overstates the forward drift by 1.85x and inverts the conclusion.
_A_ONE_DAY_MA_SLOPE_IS_NOT_A_FORWARD_PAT.mechanism: The -0.4772 one-day slope is one subtraction: the 737.95 close of 2026-06-16 left the window and 716.76 entered, a 21.19-point swap divided by 50. Nothing about that number describes the NEXT eight closes leaving the window, which are 713.65 / 710.62 / 716.38 / 706.52 / 724.08 / 736.40 / 725.17 / 712.60 -- averaging 718.18, only ~9.7 above the 708.450 replacing them. A slope is a backward-looking difference of two averages; a forward path is a schedule of known departures. They coincide only when the departing closes happen to be evenly distributed, and in a window straddling a crash-and-recovery they never are.
_A_ONE_DAY_MA_SLOPE_IS_NOT_A_FORWARD_PAT.why_this_is_the_dangerous_direction: The naive reading says a bearish break is about to self-repair, which argues for standing down or for fading it. The correct reading says the break PERSISTS on a flat tape. A run inheriting the slope-extrapolated frame would treat a live breakdown as ephemeral and dismiss a level that is in fact going to keep holding above price for at least eight sessions -- and it would do so while believing it had applied the 2026-08-25 forward-path rule, because computing a slope FEELS like computing a path. This file's most-repeated defect, a check that passes for the wrong reason, arriving inside the rule written to prevent it.
_A_ONE_DAY_MA_SLOPE_IS_NOT_A_FORWARD_PAT.detector: Never quote an MA slope as a forward drift. Roll the actual window: replace the oldest N closes one at a time with the current spot and print the resulting path. It is four lines of arithmetic on data the run already fetched. If you catch yourself dividing a distance by a one-day slope to get a number of sessions, that is the bug.
_A_ONE_DAY_MA_SLOPE_IS_NOT_A_FORWARD_PAT.companion_reading: This is the SAME MEASUREMENT the 2026-08-25T19:00Z finding made in the opposite direction -- there QQQ's 20-day carried a +1.21/day slope and a genuinely fast forward path (712.14 / 714.58 / 715.92 / 717.04) because the 07-28..07-31 crash closes were rolling out one per night. That case validated the slope; this one refutes it. The transferable point is that neither outcome is predictable from the slope itself, so the rolled window is not an optional refinement -- it is the only version of the measurement that carries information.
_A_ONE_DAY_MA_SLOPE_IS_NOT_A_FORWARD_PAT.secondary_number: QQQ's 20-day (718.7765) and 50-day (711.5868) are 7.19 apart and converging, but the same correction applies to the convergence: the naive 1.311/day closing rate implies a cross in ~5.5 sessions, while the rolled windows give 20d-minus-50d of 7.190 / 7.010 / 6.671 / 6.405 / 5.834 / 5.175 / 4.987 / 4.784 / 3.938 -- about -0.41/day, a cross nearer 17 sessions than 5.5. Do not carry the 5.5 forward.
_A_ONE_DAY_MA_SLOPE_IS_NOT_A_FORWARD_PAT.honest_scope: IT CHANGED NO DECISION, which is the only condition under which a measurement like this is creditable. The QQQ 50-day breakdown trigger was already declined twice over -- by the 16:20Z run on its volume clause (both bars, both denominators, plus the defence-versus-break ratio) and by the $302.10 capital lock, which leaves neither the CORE band nor an affordable TACTICAL vehicle. Nothing here licenses a trade in either direction; it corrects a number the next run would otherwise inherit. n=1 name, n=1 window.

_JOURNAL_LENGTH_IS_UNCORRELATED_WITH_CON.headline: THE 2026-08-30 POST-CLOSE NO-OP SCHEMA WORKS -- AND THE VOLUME IT DISPLACED REAPPEARED IN MARKET HOURS AT 14x THE SIZE, WHERE NO SCHEMA EXISTS. MEASURED: ENTRY LENGTH IS UNCORRELATED WITH WHETHER THE RUN LEARNED ANYTHING.
_JOURNAL_LENGTH_IS_UNCORRELATED_WITH_CON.the_fix_that_worked: Today's 14 post-close/overnight entries ran 533-967 bytes with one 3,653-byte exception, against the 6,771-byte mean the 2026-08-30 finding measured on trading day 2026-08-28. The six-key schema is being honoured and it cut the overnight no-op by roughly 9x. That half is a success and should not be undone.
_JOURNAL_LENGTH_IS_UNCORRELATED_WITH_CON.where_it_went: The 16 market-hours runs SINCE the 13:36Z GD fill -- across which the book did not change by a single share or contract -- wrote 181,195 bytes, mean 10,688. That is 1.58x the post-close mean the original finding called bloat, on runs that placed nothing. trade_journal.json is now 6.12 MB (1.09 MB on 2026-08-17, 5.31 MB on 2026-08-30).
_JOURNAL_LENGTH_IS_UNCORRELATED_WITH_CON.the_measurement_that_makes_it_actionable: Splitting those 16 by whether the run produced a NEW dated durable key in holdings.json: WITH a durable finding, n=8, mean 10,513 bytes. WITHOUT one, n=8, mean 10,864 bytes. Runs that learned nothing wrote SLIGHTLY LONGER entries than runs that learned something. Length is therefore not being driven by content -- it is a habit of the format.
_JOURNAL_LENGTH_IS_UNCORRELATED_WITH_CON.hypothesis_tested_and_REFUTED: The obvious explanation -- that long journal entries are restating the holdings.json findings written the same run -- is FALSE. Checked by sentence-matching three run/key pairs (16:30Z vs _A_ONE_DAY_MA_SLOPE_IS_NOT_A_FORWARD_PATH, 16:00Z vs _BAND_FLOOR_REACHED_IS_NOT_VEHICLE_AFFORDABLE, 15:15Z vs _DIRECTION_RULE_SUBSTITUTION_IS_A_FLOOR): 53 key sentences over 60 chars, ZERO appearing in the paired entry. The two artifacts are not duplicates. Recorded as refuted rather than quietly dropped, per the 16:05Z precedent -- a run that only writes up its confirmed guesses is a run whose write-ups cannot be trusted.
_JOURNAL_LENGTH_IS_UNCORRELATED_WITH_CON.what_it_actually_is: Re-derivation. Each run re-states the regime, the capital arithmetic, the rotation gate and six position verdicts in full prose, all of which are unchanged and all of which already live in _current_state_run -- the object the ledger-notes rule says to OVERWRITE IN PLACE precisely so the journal does not have to carry them.
_JOURNAL_LENGTH_IS_UNCORRELATED_WITH_CON.remedy_MARKET_HOURS_RE_VERIFICATION_SCHE: When a market-hours run changes nothing in either book AND produces no new durable finding, write these keys and stop: run_utc, run_type, trading_day_et, headline (one sentence), reconciliation (one line: option qty, equity count, cash/total, drift), tape (numbers only, no verdict -- the 2026-08-31 lesson), why_flat (one line per book), duties (one line). Target under ~1,500 bytes. The full write-up is earned by a FILL, an EXIT, or a NEW DURABLE FINDING -- and the finding itself belongs in a holdings.json key, with the journal entry naming it rather than re-arguing it.
_JOURNAL_LENGTH_IS_UNCORRELATED_WITH_CON.detector: len(json.dumps(entry)) before committing. Over ~1,500 bytes on a market-hours run that placed nothing and learned nothing means you are re-deriving, not reporting. Same shape as the git diff --stat rule: trust the byte count, not your sense of having been concise.
_JOURNAL_LENGTH_IS_UNCORRELATED_WITH_CON.transferable_lesson: A schema fixes the presentation it names, and the behaviour migrates to the presentation it does not. The 2026-08-30 rule was scoped to run_type post_close_overnight; nothing was written for market_hours_regular, so the habit simply moved there and grew. This file's most-repeated shape -- a rule that names one instance of a defect instead of its class -- arriving inside the rule written to stop it.
_JOURNAL_LENGTH_IS_UNCORRELATED_WITH_CON.honest_scope: This changed no trading decision and could not have: the book was flat on every gate before it was measured. n=8 per arm is small and the two means are 3% apart, so the claim is NOT that runs without findings write more -- it is that there is NO relationship in either direction, which is the whole point. Market-hours runs legitimately do more work than overnight ones (live quotes, tape measurement, hunt grading), so some length is earned; the 8 runs that earned none wrote the same amount anyway. This entry is written to the schema it proposes.

_CATALYST_WINDOW_OVER_INCLUSION_ON_A_TUE.HEADLINE: The 2026-08-28 rule says SCREEN THE CATALYST WINDOW AGAINST THIS TRACK'S HOLD PERIOD. Four consecutive runs (17:30Z, 17:45Z, 18:00Z, 18:15Z) then wrote that PANW/DELL/CRDO/MDB tonight AND AVGO/SNOW/HPE/NTAP on 09-02 are 'both inside a Tuesday scalp's hold window'. Verified against get_earnings_calendar: the second cluster is NOT.
_CATALYST_WINDOW_OVER_INCLUSION_ON_A_TUE.the_arithmetic: A TACTICAL scalp entered Tuesday 2026-09-01 has a hard time stop of FLAT BY THE CLOSE OF THE NEXT SESSION = Wednesday 2026-09-02's bell. Calendar, verified this run: PANW / DELL / CRDO / MDB / GTLB all report 2026-09-01 pm -- INSIDE the window, the position is held across them. AVGO / SNOW / HPE / NTAP all report 2026-09-02 pm -- OUTSIDE it by minutes, since the position must already be flat at that day's close. Wednesday's own session is comparatively clean: the 09-02 am names are OLLI, FCEL, BF.B, CXM, GIII, REX, REVG, none index-moving.
_CATALYST_WINDOW_OVER_INCLUSION_ON_A_TUE.the_defect_class: This is the SAME finding the 2026-08-28T15:35Z rule records, arriving from the OPPOSITE direction. That case was BORROWING another track's catalyst list (a CORE objection cited against a scalp). This case is OVER-INCLUSION within the correct track -- extending the window one session past the time stop. Both produce a decline reached for a reason that does not apply, and both are invisible because the decline itself is correct.
_CATALYST_WINDOW_OVER_INCLUSION_ON_A_TUE.why_it_survived_four_runs: The objection is right ONE DAY EARLY. A scalp entered WEDNESDAY 09-02 genuinely does carry AVGO/SNOW/HPE/NTAP inside its window. An error of timing rather than of substance reads as correct on every re-verification, and each run inherited the phrasing rather than re-deriving the window against the calendar.
_CATALYST_WINDOW_OVER_INCLUSION_ON_A_TUE.honest_scope_it_changed_no_decision: TACTICAL stays declined on two INDEPENDENT grounds that survive the correction in full: (1) tonight's 09-01 pm cluster is genuinely inside the window, which alone satisfies the 2026-08-26 regime capstone; (2) affordability -- deployable is $302.10 against a $300-1,000 band, i.e. $2.10 of headroom, and no 0.40-0.60 delta vehicle on SPY/QQQ/NVDA has priced under $302 in any measurement this desk has logged. Chain deliberately NOT re-quoted: a re-price cannot change a decision already made on the capstone. A catalyst screen can only be audited credibly on a run where the audit does not license a trade.
_CATALYST_WINDOW_OVER_INCLUSION_ON_A_TUE.forward_cost_if_uncorrected: A run inheriting 'AVGO is in my window' declines a WEDNESDAY-MORNING scalp on a catalyst that is by then correctly inside it, and would decline a THURSDAY-morning one on the same phrase when it is by then fully resolved. The error inverts from over-strict to over-permissive as the phrase ages.

_HEDGE_MAKES_THE_BOOK_NET_SHORT_DESPITE_.why_it_is_decision_relevant: It cuts AGAINST the standing reflex. Twenty-six runs today have declined equity entries, and the unstated frame behind a selloff decline is 'adding long exposure now adds risk'. On the measured posture the opposite is true at the margin: a new long moves this book TOWARD neutral, not toward risk. The desk has never made that argument because it had never measured the hedge's delta against the current book.
_HEDGE_MAKES_THE_BOOK_NET_SHORT_DESPITE_.THE_GUARD_THAT_KEEPS_IT_FROM_BECOMING_A_: 'The hedge makes new equity entries safer' is exactly the shape of argument that talks a desk into a marginal trade, so bound it explicitly: (a) the hedge is a FIXED $749 of insurance with ~80 DTE, it does not scale with anything added underneath it; (b) its delta shrinks precisely in the rally where a fresh long would need no protection and grows in the selloff where the long is already losing -- the protection is anti-correlated with the need in the wrong way for a NEW position; (c) it therefore informs SIZING CONTEXT only and NEVER the entry bar. A B-grade setup does not become A-grade because the book is hedged. The A-grade-only bar, HARD RULE 7, the rotation gate and FOUR LAWS #4 are untouched by this measurement.

_ROTATION_GATE_IS_ANSWERABLE_FROM_THE_SC.headline: WHEN HELD POSITIONS APPEAR ON THE SAME SCREEN AS THE CANDIDATES, THE SCREEN'S OWN RANKING IS A DIRECT ANSWER TO THE ROTATION GATE -- AND IT DISPOSES OF MOST OF THE LIST WITHOUT AN INDIVIDUAL WORKUP.
_ROTATION_GATE_IS_ANSWERABLE_FROM_THE_SC.context: The full-deployment capital policy (CLAUDE.md, Ryan 2026-08-29) replaced the 45% floor with mechanic #3: once deployable cash is below one normal position size, a new idea must be graded BETTER THAN THE WEAKEST POSITION CURRENTLY HELD, and funding it means selling that position. Deployable was $302.10 against a $400-500 normal size, so the gate was live. Every run since 08-29 has answered it in PROSE ('no held name is weakest on the entry stack'), which is true but unfalsifiable and cannot be audited by the next instance.
_ROTATION_GATE_IS_ANSWERABLE_FROM_THE_SC.measurement: The committed 19:02Z intraday report lists 34 RSI(2) setups ordered by RSI2. FOUR of them are positions the book already holds: MMM #4 (RSI2 1.4), MDLZ #6 (1.7), PNC #7 (1.7), GD #18 (4.5). So 30 of 34 candidates rank BELOW a name already owned. Buying any of those 30 means selling a better-ranked, intact-thesis position to fund a worse-ranked one, which is the churn the rotation rule's own wording forbids ('weakest' means weakest on the ENTRY STACK, never simply the biggest loser).

the_three_that_needed_a_real_grade.AEHR_rank_1_rsi2_0.2: DECLINED, grade C. Suggested invalidation sits 18.1% below spot -- on a book that places no price stops, an 18% thesis-death level is not a tight mean-reversion trade but a small-cap semi with wide dispersion. Compounded by direct AVGO-complex beta into the 09-02 pm print (the same-complex earnings rule treats a dominant peer print as an [ERN] flag even with no own print).
the_three_that_needed_a_real_grade.AMAT_rank_3_rsi2_1.3: DEFERRED, not excluded. Clean setup, -6.8% invalidation, no own earnings, but core semi-cap equipment with AVGO reporting 09-02 pm, squarely inside a 1-3 week hold. The deferral EXPIRES with the event: re-grade from scratch on post-print numbers and never reuse today's grade -- a gap-up can consume a mean-reversion edge as easily as a gap-down creates one.
the_three_that_needed_a_real_grade.UNP_rank_2_rsi2_1.0: DECLINED on the rotation gate, and it is the honest case. Genuinely clean -- rails, no earnings in the window, -3.2% invalidation, +4.7% to target, no sector-steer conflict. Funding it means selling MMM (#4, entered 08-31, thesis intact, -1.50%). The entire edge on offer is 0.4 of an RSI2 point, inside the noise of a 2-period oscillator. Paying a round trip and realizing a loss on an intact thesis for that is churn wearing a rotation's clothes.

_ROTATION_GATE_IS_ANSWERABLE_FROM_THE_SC.honest_limit_read_this_before_reusing_it: RSI2 rank is the OVERSOLD TRIGGER ONLY. It says nothing about thesis strength, trend quality, invalidation distance, sector concentration or earnings -- all of which are part of the entry stack the rotation rule actually names. A candidate ranked below a held name could still be the better position on the full stack. What the ranking legitimately does is ORDER THE WORKUP: it identifies the handful that could possibly clear the bar so the desk grades those properly instead of writing up thirty names. Used as a screen it is sound; used as a VERDICT it would be exactly the 'check that passes for the wrong reason' this file keeps catching. Never let it substitute for the HARD RULE 7 thesis gate on a name actually being bought.
_ROTATION_GATE_IS_ANSWERABLE_FROM_THE_SC.why_it_generalizes: The gate asks a COMPARATIVE question, and until now the desk answered it with an absolute one ('is this setup A-grade?'). Any screen that ranks candidates and also surfaces held names hands the comparison over for free -- no extra call, no extra judgement. It also makes the answer auditable: a future run can check '30 of 34' against the committed report, which it cannot do with 'no held name is weakest'.

THE TRANSFERABLE SHAPE, which is this file's most-repeated one: a dedup key built from a field that is not universal across the file's history looks correct on every entry it was designed against and silently deletes the ones it was not. Nothing errors, the merge succeeds, and the loss is invisible unless the count is asserted -- a check that passes for the wrong reason. Same family as the git diff --stat rule and the options lot invariants: trust the assertion, not your reading of the merge. _FEED_DRIFT_IS_ONE_DIRECTIONAL_SO_THE_AB.status: DURABLE. Refines the 2026-08-28T14:20Z direction rule (a bucket materially BELOW its 1-minute sum = bucket holed, use the sum; materially ABOVE = 1-minute series holed, keep the bucket). The BELOW branch is confirmed again here. The ABOVE branch, applied on the gap alone, fires on ordinary drift.
_FEED_DRIFT_IS_ONE_DIRECTIONAL_SO_THE_AB.the_measurement: Ten bucket-vs-1-minute-sum reconciliations across SPY and QQQ, 19:05-19:29Z. Two were genuine holes (SPY 19:10 -55.08%, QQQ 19:10 -66.38%, agreeing at one timestamp = the cross-symbol feed-window signature). The other EIGHT were all POSITIVE, none negative: +1.56, +2.97, +6.81, +6.90, +2.11, +0.42, +0.19, +0.00 percent.
_FEED_DRIFT_IS_ONE_DIRECTIONAL_SO_THE_AB.the_finding: DRIFT IS ONE-DIRECTIONAL. A 5-minute bucket settles ABOVE its 1-minute sum as late prints land, never below. So the two branches of the direction rule do NOT sit in symmetric noise: the BELOW branch is clean-signal, because ordinary drift never points that way and any negative gap is a hole. The ABOVE branch sits directly on top of the entire drift distribution, so a fixed ~5% tolerance will keep classifying drift as a 1-minute hole.
_FEED_DRIFT_IS_ONE_DIRECTIONAL_SO_THE_AB.measured_here: SPY's 19:20 (+6.81%) and 19:25 (+6.90%) buckets exceed the stated ~5% tolerance and the rule as written declares the 1-minute series holed. They are almost certainly NOT: neither window contains a minute bar that is a tiny fraction of both neighbours (19:20-24 = 42334/45096/29212/36483/23081; 19:25-29 = 31859/26112/38915/42729/50822 -- no hole signature), and QQQ read +0.19% and +0.00% in the IDENTICAL windows, so there is no cross-symbol agreement. Drift on one symbol, running a couple of points above the +4.4% the 2026-08-28 sample had seen.
_FEED_DRIFT_IS_ONE_DIRECTIONAL_SO_THE_AB.the_rule: Declare a 1-minute hole only on the gap PLUS corroboration: either a minute bar that is a tiny fraction of BOTH its neighbours, or the same timestamp gapping on a second symbol (free -- the tool takes 10 symbols per call). Absent corroboration, a positive gap is drift: keep the bucket, and note the drift rather than naming a defect. The BELOW branch needs no corroboration and keeps its bare-gap test.
_FEED_DRIFT_IS_ONE_DIRECTIONAL_SO_THE_AB.why_it_matters_and_why_it_is_small: It is the SAFE direction of the two -- the ABOVE branch's remedy is 'keep the bucket', which is what you would do anyway, so a false positive here costs a wrong label in the journal, not a wrong denominator. Recorded because a mislabelled defect propagates: the next run inherits 'the 1-minute series was holed at 19:20Z' as a measured fact and reasons from it. Same family as every other entry here -- a detector that has only seen its failure mode point one way encodes that direction as the mechanism.
_FEED_DRIFT_IS_ONE_DIRECTIONAL_SO_THE_AB.honest_scope: n=10 reconciliations on one session, two symbols. The claim that drift is one-directional is well-supported by 8-for-8 positive here and is consistent with the 2026-08-28 sample (+3.7%, +1.74%, +0.04% to +4.1%, all positive), but no run has yet checked it on a slow-tape session. CHANGED NO DECISION: no volume clause was load-bearing this run -- no trigger fired and TACTICAL was declined on capital and overnight carry before any baseline was computed.

_OPENING_WINDOW_IV_DISCOUNT_IS_A_FUNCTIO.headline: THE -2.5% TO -4.4% OPENING-WINDOW ATM IV DISCOUNT IS A DECAY CURVE, NOT A CONSTANT -- AT +29 MINUTES IT HAS BARELY STARTED, AND APPLYING THE FULL BAND THERE OVER-CORRECTS BY ROUGHLY ITS OWN SIZE. MEASURED 2026-09-02T14:02Z ON FOUR SAME-STRIKE NAMES.
_OPENING_WINDOW_IV_DISCOUNT_IS_A_FUNCTIO.measurement: 13:33Z sweep re-quoted at 14:02-14:03Z, same 2026-10-02 board, restricted to the names whose ATM strike did NOT move so skew cannot contaminate the reading: QQQ 706 -0.72%, NVDA 220 +1.36%, TSM 415 -0.55%, AVGO re-quoted at its morning 365 strike -0.82%. _OPENING_WINDOW_IV_DISCOUNT_IS_A_FUNCTIO.mechanism: The band's own readings were taken at +66 min (SPY, QQQ at 14:47Z), +110 min (NVDA at 15:31Z) and a similar settled hour on 2026-08-27. Today's is +29 min. The wide auction markets that inflate an ATM IV read tighten CONTINUOUSLY after the bell, so the correction is a function of elapsed time and the band measures its asymptote, not its value at an arbitrary earlier moment. Nothing here contradicts the band; it bounds WHEN the band applies.
_OPENING_WINDOW_IV_DISCOUNT_IS_A_FUNCTIO.rule: Do NOT subtract a flat 2.5-4.4% from an ATM row re-read less than ~45 minutes after the open. Either re-quote and MEASURE the artifact on a same-strike contract -- it costs one call and is exact -- or state the discount as unmeasured. An artifact you have not measured is not an explanation.

That row read AVGO's ex-gap 1.5238 -- the highest AVGO value in iv_history.json -- declared 'the whole increment sits INSIDE the artifact', and handed forward 'the honest read is FLAT day-over-day, not richest ever'. Measured on AVGO's own 365 strike the artifact is -0.82%, about a fifth of the increment. The settled, time-matched reading is a genuine file high: ex-gap 1.5202 at the method-correct 370 strike (+3.83% over yesterday's 1.4641) or 1.5113 at the morning's 365 strike (+3.22%). A run that had merely applied the documented band by rote would have deleted a real observation about event premium on the eve of AVGO's print.
_OPENING_WINDOW_IV_DISCOUNT_IS_A_FUNCTIO.the_shape: This file's most-repeated defect arriving from the OPPOSITE side. The usual form is a check that passes for the wrong reason; here a CORRECTION was applied for the wrong reason -- rotely, from a remembered constant, without measuring the thing it was correcting for. A rule written to stop a run manufacturing a vol-bid story out of a clock difference was itself capable of manufacturing a flat reading out of one. Corrections need the same evidentiary bar as the claims they overturn.
_OPENING_WINDOW_IV_DISCOUNT_IS_A_FUNCTIO.detail_worth_keeping: The one name that APPEARED to confirm the band today is SPY at -2.74% -- and SPY is a name whose ATM strike moved 762 -> 764, so that reading is skew, not settling. The confounded name is the one that looked like corroboration. Restrict any artifact measurement to same-strike pairs.
_OPENING_WINDOW_IV_DISCOUNT_IS_A_FUNCTIO.honest_scope: n=4, one session, one 29-minute interval. This does NOT refute the band and must not be cited as doing so -- it is untested today whether the full -2.5% to -4.4% appears by 14:45Z, which is where the band's own readings live. What is established is narrower and firmer: the discount is not present at +29 minutes, so the elapsed time is load-bearing and a fixed constant is the wrong shape for it. It changed no trade -- both books were capital-blocked before the sweep began -- which is the only condition under which a measurement method can be audited credibly.

_REPORT_RSI2_ON_HELD_NAMES_IS_A_LIVE_OVE.THE_RULE: TREAT THE REPORT'S RSI2 ON A HELD NAME AS A LIVE QUOTE, NOT AS A FACT. USB is the honest counter-case and must not be waved away: one of the four genuinely healed and kept going. So the defensible claim is NOT that departure predicts further decline -- it is that departure carries NO information in expectation, which is exactly what the original finding said and what a 1-of-4 hit rate on a distributing tape is consistent with. Anyone reading this as 'names that leave the screen fall' has inverted a null result into a signal, which is the same error the original finding was written to stop.
