_ROTATION_SELL_SIDE_IS_THE_GREEN_NAME_NO.headline: THE MAGNITUDE FLOOR'S OWN ESCAPE HATCH -- 'a graded ROTATION reason' -- MAKES THE GREEN, OVERBOUGHT NAME THE NATURAL ROTATION SELL SIDE, WHICH IS THE ONE FRAMING EIGHT CONSECUTIVE DECLINES NEVER TESTED. TESTED HERE ON ROST AGAINST SIX FRESH CANDIDATES. IT DECLINES -- BUT ON ARITHMETIC, NOT ON THE ABSENCE OF A SELL SIDE.
_ROTATION_SELL_SIDE_IS_THE_GREEN_NAME_NO.status: DURABLE. Changed no decision (the rotation declines and ROST holds), which is the only condition under which a gate's own reasoning can be audited credibly.
_ROTATION_SELL_SIDE_IS_THE_GREEN_NAME_NO.what_every_prior_run_asserted: Runs from 2026-08-29 onward answered the rotation gate with 'no held name has a thesis break to supply the sell side.' True, and it silently assumed the sell side must be an UNDERWATER name freed by a thesis break. It need not be. _MECHANICAL_EXIT_HAS_NO_MAGNITUDE_FLOOR states the alternative in its own rule text: below the one-third floor the RSI2>=70 print is 'an OPTIONAL exit-into-strength ... which needs a HARD RULE 7 thesis break OR A GRADED ROTATION REASON.' ROST is green, overbought (RSI2 83.2), report-flagged SELL, and carries no thesis question at all -- so it is the one position whose exit requires NO thesis break, only a candidate that grades better. Eight runs declined the ROST exit without ever asking whether a rotation reason existed.
_ROTATION_SELL_SIDE_IS_THE_GREEN_NAME_NO.why_it_matters_beyond_this_name: The two rules compose in a way neither states alone. The magnitude floor blocks banking a trivial gain on a bare technical trigger; the rotation gate blocks funding a new idea without a sell side. Read together they do NOT deadlock -- the floor names rotation as a valid trigger, and the green name is the cheapest sell side available because selling it realizes a GAIN rather than the churn HARD RULE 5 forbids ('selling a sound underwater thesis to chase a fresher signal'). A desk that only ever looks for the sell side among its losers will never find one, because an intact underwater thesis is exactly what the rule protects.
_ROTATION_SELL_SIDE_IS_THE_GREEN_NAME_NO.the_test_that_decides_it: Compare the held name's REMAINING upside to the candidate's TOTAL upside, both to their written targets, then check the candidate's trigger rank and invalidation width. ROST live 232.595 -> target 244.66 = +5.19% remaining. The six candidates new to the 17:02Z report and never graded by any prior run: UNP +4.58% (rank 3), GS +5.55% (rank 9), MS +3.54% (rank 15), NBIS +34.69% (rank 18), PANW +17.08% (rank 22), CSCO +8.13% (rank 23).
_ROTATION_SELL_SIDE_IS_THE_GREEN_NAME_NO.verdict_declined_and_why: NO candidate is simultaneously better-ranked on the oversold trigger AND offering more upside than ROST's remaining AND carrying a tolerable invalidation. UNP is the closest and fails on arithmetic: +4.58% total is LESS than ROST's +5.19% remaining, and its edge over MMM is 0.2 of an RSI2 point (down from the 0.4 that already declined it on 2026-09-01). GS/CSCO offer marginally more upside but rank 9th and dead-last 23rd on the trigger that is the entry's whole premise. NBIS and PANW offer the most upside solely because they are the most volatile -- invalidations 23.1% and 11.4% below spot, and in a book that places NO price stops a wide invalidation is a real negative, the identical objection that graded AEHR a C on 2026-09-01.
_ROTATION_SELL_SIDE_IS_THE_GREEN_NAME_NO.the_honest_counter_argument: ROST at RSI2 83.2 is extended, so the probability of it walking to 244.66 is plausibly lower than a fresh oversold name reaching its own target -- the remaining-vs-total comparison silently treats both as equally likely and they are not. That cuts against holding. It is recorded rather than resolved because nothing here measures it, and because HARD RULE 5 settles the tie the other way: winners are managed by target and trail, never sold pre-emptively on being extended. If a future run can measure hit rates by RSI2 level at decision time, this is the assumption to attack first.
_ROTATION_SELL_SIDE_IS_THE_GREEN_NAME_NO.detector: When the magnitude floor declines a take-profit, do not stop at 'no sell side exists.' The declined name IS a sell-side candidate. Run the remaining-vs-total upside test against every ungraded candidate before writing the decline, and say which of the two reasons is doing the work: no rotation reason graded out, or no sell side existed at all. They are different findings and only the first is auditable.

_REPORT_REWARD_RISK_IS_AN_ARTIFACT_OF_TA.headline: 15 OF THE 23 RSI2 SETUPS IN THE 17:02Z REPORT SIT AT EXACTLY 1.50 REWARD/RISK, MEDIAN 1.500. THE TARGET AND STOP ARE BOTH DERIVED FROM THE SAME VOLATILITY ESTIMATE, SO R:R IS LARGELY A CONSTANT OF CONSTRUCTION AND CARRIES NEAR-ZERO INFORMATION FOR RANKING CANDIDATES.
_REPORT_REWARD_RISK_IS_AN_ARTIFACT_OF_TA.measurement: Computed over all 23 setups in the committed 2026-09-02T17:02Z latest_intraday.md: mean 1.647, median 1.500, population stdev 0.359, min 1.069 (MS), max 2.519 (MMM). Exactly 1.50 on BLK, UNP, FDX, GS, MRVL, LRCX, DDOG, GLW, NBIS, SNOW, AAOI, PANW, CSCO plus GM and IBKR at 1.49 (rounding) = 15 of 23. The eight that deviate cluster in two groups: five ABOVE 2.0 (MMM 2.52, RTX 2.34, FCEL 2.28, GD 2.27, AMAT 2.03) and three at or below 1.56 but off the mode (GE 1.56, NOK 1.32, MS 1.07).
_REPORT_REWARD_RISK_IS_AN_ARTIFACT_OF_TA.the_trap_it_disarms: A candidate offering '+34.7% to target' looks dramatically better than one offering '+4.6%' until the stop is read alongside it: NBIS is +34.69%/-23.13% and UNP is +4.58%/-3.06%, and both are 1.50. The bigger number is not a better trade, it is a more volatile name wearing a proportionally wider invalidation. Ranking candidates on upside-to-target -- which is the most natural thing to do when scanning the table -- systematically sorts the list by volatility and calls it opportunity.
_REPORT_REWARD_RISK_IS_AN_ARTIFACT_OF_TA.what_still_discriminates: The oversold trigger rank (RSI2), the HARD RULE 7 thesis, the sector steer, the earnings window, and INVALIDATION WIDTH IN ABSOLUTE TERMS. The last is the one the ratio actively hides and it matters most here, because this book places NO price stops (HARD RULE 5): a 23% invalidation is not 1.50-R risk, it is a name whose thesis-death level is a quarter of the position away, which is why AEHR was graded C on 2026-09-01 on exactly this ground.
_REPORT_REWARD_RISK_IS_AN_ARTIFACT_OF_TA.honest_scope: One report snapshot, n=23, and the deviating eight are not explained -- both HELD names (MMM, GD) sit in the high group, which hints the ratio distorts once live price has drifted from the report's own entry estimate, but that is a hypothesis and was not tested. The claim made is narrow: the modal value is exactly 1.50 at 65% frequency, so R:R must not be used as a ranking input. It is not a claim that the report's targets are wrong.

_EXTENDED_IS_NOT_LESS_LIKELY_TO_REACH_TA.headline: THE ONE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT LEFT OPEN AGAINST HOLDING ROST -- 'an extended name is less likely to walk to its target than a fresh oversold one, so the remaining-vs-total upside comparison silently treats unequal probabilities as equal' -- IS MEASURED AND DOES NOT HOLD ON ROST'S OWN THREE-YEAR HISTORY. The extended cohort reaches +5.19% intrabar 38.0% of the time over 15 sessions; the oversold cohort 39.8%. Essentially a tie, and the extended cohort has the HIGHER mean and a far higher median.
_EXTENDED_IS_NOT_LESS_LIKELY_TO_REACH_TA.status: DURABLE. Changed no decision -- ROST holds under both the magnitude floor and the rotation gate regardless -- which is the only condition under which a gate's own assumption can be audited credibly.
_EXTENDED_IS_NOT_LESS_LIKELY_TO_REACH_TA.what_it_answers: The _ROTATION_SELL_SIDE_IS_THE_GREEN_NAME_NOT_THE_WEAKEST_LOSER key (17:15Z) declined the ROST rotation on arithmetic and then recorded its own weakness: 'ROST at RSI2 83.2 is extended, so the probability of it walking to 244.66 is plausibly lower than a fresh oversold name reaching its own target -- the remaining-vs-total comparison silently treats both as equal probability.' That is a probability claim, and it had never been given a number. It has one now.
_EXTENDED_IS_NOT_LESS_LIKELY_TO_REACH_TA.method: get_equity_historicals(ROST, day, split-adjusted, 2023-09-01..2026-09-01) = 752 daily bars. Wilder RSI(2) computed on closes. VALIDATION FIRST: the implementation returns 35.547 on the 2026-09-01 settled close, reproducing to three decimals the value _MAGNITUDE_FLOOR_FIRST_LIVE_APPLICATION measured independently at 15:02Z via get_equity_technical_indicators. Two different sources, same number -- the oscillator is not the uncertain part of this. Cohorts: EXTENDED = every bar with RSI2>=80 (n=213), OVERSOLD = every bar with RSI2<10 (n=90, the state a fresh screen candidate is in). Forward close-to-close returns at 5/10/15 sessions, plus whether the intrabar HIGH reached +5.19% -- ROST's actual remaining distance to its 244.66 target -- inside the horizon.
_EXTENDED_IS_NOT_LESS_LIKELY_TO_REACH_TA.the_finding: At the 15-session horizon that matches the 1-3 week swing hold, the two cohorts reach ROST's own remaining objective at 38.0% vs 39.8% -- a 1.8-point gap on overlapping samples, which is noise. On central tendency the EXTENDED state is the better one, not the worse: mean +1.20% vs +0.92%, median +1.85% vs -0.02%, positive 60.6% vs 49.4%. So the equal-probability assumption the rotation arithmetic rests on is approximately correct for the reach test, and if it is biased at all it is biased AGAINST the held name -- i.e. the 17:15Z decline was, if anything, conservative.
_EXTENDED_IS_NOT_LESS_LIKELY_TO_REACH_TA.the_second_result_which_is_the_uncomfort: The OVERSOLD cohort's MEDIAN 15-session forward return on this name is -0.02% -- the RSI2<10 entry trigger, on ROST's own three years, has a coin-flip median. Its mean is positive only because the right tail carries it (39.8% of instances touch +5.19% at some point). That is not a condemnation of the screen: it is one name, the sample overlaps heavily, and the desk's entries add a rising-200-day-MA gate this cohort does not. But it is the first time this desk has put a base rate under the entry signal at all, and the honest reading is that the RSI2 edge here is a right-tail edge, not a central-tendency one -- which is exactly the shape that makes a hold-to-target policy correct and a bank-a-small-gain policy wrong. It independently supports the magnitude floor from a direction the floor's own derivation never used.
_EXTENDED_IS_NOT_LESS_LIKELY_TO_REACH_TA.honest_scope: ONE NAME, IN-SAMPLE ON THE VERY POSITION BEING DECIDED -- the weakest possible evidential posture, and it must not be cited as a general law about RSI2. The 213 and 83 observations are heavily OVERLAPPING (RSI2 extremes cluster in runs), so effective n is a small fraction of the nominal count and no significance test is offered or implied. ROST trended up over much of the 2023-2026 window, which lifts every cohort's forward return and inflates both reach rates. What is established is narrow and sufficient for its purpose: the specific probability asymmetry that was asserted as a caveat against holding ROST is not visible in ROST's own data, so it cannot carry the rotation decision either way.
_EXTENDED_IS_NOT_LESS_LIKELY_TO_REACH_TA.what_would_generalize_it: Run the identical two-cohort split across the report's RSI2 universe rather than one name, with non-overlapping sampling (one observation per signal run, not per bar), and with the rising-200-day-MA gate applied so the OVERSOLD cohort matches what the desk actually enters. That is a real backtest and belongs in a post-close run, not a 15-minute market-hours slot.

_SETTLE_MECHANICAL_EXITS_BEFORE_COMPUTIN.headline: AN ORDERING DEFECT, NOT A RULE CONFLICT: THE ROTATION GATE WAS DISPOSING OF THE WHOLE SCREEN ON THE PREMISE THAT FUNDING REQUIRES A ROTATION SELL, WHILE ROST CARRIED A LIVE, AUTHORIZED MECHANICAL EXIT THAT WOULD HAVE SUPPLIED FUNDING WITH NO ROTATION AT ALL. EACH DECISION WAS DEFENSIBLE ALONE; TOGETHER THEY LOCKED THE BOOK.

the_two_halves.half_1: The capital gate reads deployable $302.10 (cash $552.10 minus the $250 reserve), below one normal position size, so the full-deployment policy's mechanism 3 engages: a new idea must be graded BETTER THAN THE WEAKEST POSITION HELD, and the rotation sell must clear HARD RULE 7 and the ownership gate. With no held name showing a thesis break, no sell side exists -- so the ranking screen disposes of every candidate ranking below a held name WITHOUT EVER GRADING IT ON MERIT.
the_two_halves.half_2: ROST's mechanical take-profit is FIRED and AUTHORIZED in its own right -- RSI2 >= 70 with price > entry, which HARD RULE 5 and prompt v8 both make an autonomous banking authority, and which the 2026-08-26 profit-banking correction confirms is available precisely because ROST is GREEN. Banking it is NOT a rotation sell and needs no thesis break. It would take cash $552.10 -> ~$1,016 and deployable $302.10 -> ~$766, ABOVE one normal position size -- at which point the rotation gate no longer governs and the ordinary A-grade bar does.

_SETTLE_MECHANICAL_EXITS_BEFORE_COMPUTIN.the_defect: The two were being evaluated in the wrong order and in isolation from each other. Capital was treated as FIXED at $302.10 while the screen was disposed of; ROST was declined separately on its own magnitude floor. Neither run was wrong on its own question. But the conjunction asserts something no run actually established: that the book had no fundable entry, when in fact it held an authorized, unexercised route to funding one.
_SETTLE_MECHANICAL_EXITS_BEFORE_COMPUTIN.the_correct_sequence: 1. Settle every AUTHORIZED MECHANICAL EXIT on its own merits first (target hit / RSI2>=70 while green), independently of what it might fund -- deciding an exit by reference to the entry it enables is fitting the exit to the trade, the reasoning error this file repeatedly forbids. 2. THEN compute the capital gate on the resulting cash. 3. Apply the rotation gate ONLY if deployable is still below one position size. Grading the screen against a capital number that an unexercised exit authority can change is measuring against a stale denominator -- the same family as every other denominator defect in this file.
_SETTLE_MECHANICAL_EXITS_BEFORE_COMPUTIN.tested_today_and_it_changed_nothing_whic: Run in the correct order: UNP is the only un-disposed candidate, and it grades C on the measured rail de-rate above. AMAT/MRVL/LRCX stay deferred on AVGO tonight (independent of funding). FCEL/SNOW/FDX excluded on earnings, MMM/GD held. So there is no A-grade name, banking ROST would free capital with nothing to deploy into, and ROST is held on its own magnitude floor exactly as before. A process audit is only credible on a run where the audit does not license a trade.
_SETTLE_MECHANICAL_EXITS_BEFORE_COMPUTIN.but_it_would_have_mattered: On any day the screen produces an A-grade name, the old ordering returns 'no compliant entry' while the new ordering returns a funded trade. That is the whole cost of the defect, and it is invisible on days like this one.

_RSI2_EXIT_TRIGGER_SITS_AT_THE_ENTRY_PRI.the_mechanism_which_is_the_transferable_: A 2-period RSI's full traverse from oversold to overbought spans only the last few sessions' range. The ENTRY is taken when RSI2 is near its floor -- i.e. at a point inside that range -- and the EXIT fires when RSI2 reaches 70, which requires only that price recover to roughly the same range. Both prices are drawn from the SAME short window, so they coincide. This is why the trigger tracks the recent range rather than the entry: on names that have drifted down since entry (PNC -1.8%, LLY -1.2%) the trigger has drifted BELOW the entry with them; on names entered nearer their low (MMM, GD) it sits slightly above. THE TRIGGER PRICE IS ALWAYS 'ROUGHLY WHERE THE STOCK HAS RECENTLY BEEN', NEVER 'ENTRY PLUS A PROFIT'.
_RSI2_EXIT_TRIGGER_SITS_AT_THE_ENTRY_PRI.what_this_does_to_the_18_05Z_FLAG_and_it: The 18:05Z flag's core objection was that the magnitude floor's DENOMINATOR is a number the report itself labels an ESTIMATE, so eleven exits had been declined against a benchmark the source disclaims. That objection is now MOOT: the trigger sits at the entry price by construction, so the mechanical exit banks ~0-1% of position value WHATEVER the target is. The floor does not need the target to justify itself, and the argument no longer rests on an advisory number. The floor is not an ad-hoc override the desk keeps reaching for -- it is correcting a STRUCTURAL property of pairing an RSI2 entry screen with an RSI2 exit trigger, and it will therefore fire on essentially every position this book ever takes.
_RSI2_EXIT_TRIGGER_SITS_AT_THE_ENTRY_PRI.the_honest_counter_argument_and_it_is_st: CONNORS' OWN RSI(2) METHOD USES THE CROSS BACK ABOVE ~70 AS THE DESIGNED EXIT AND PROMISES NO TARGET. Under the pure method, 'exit at approximately breakeven-to-small-gain, frequently' is not a defect -- it is the strategy: you compound via a high hit rate on many small gains, not via large per-trade objectives. So this measurement does NOT establish that the mechanical exit is wrong. It establishes something narrower and more useful, below.
_RSI2_EXIT_TRIGGER_SITS_AT_THE_ENTRY_PRI.THE_ACTUAL_GOVERNANCE_QUESTION_restated_: THIS BOOK IS RUNNING TWO DIFFERENT EXIT SYSTEMS AT ONCE AND THEY DISAGREE BY CONSTRUCTION. The ledger records a TARGET for every swing (ROST 244.66, MDLZ 64.70, ...) and the report prints it; the automation executes the RSI2>=70 CROSS. Measured above, those two exits are ~0.8% and ~6% apart in price terms and 5x-35x apart in payoff. Pick ONE: (a) TARGET-BASED -- the RSI2>=70 print is advisory, exits happen on the target, the trailing stop, or a thesis break, and the magnitude floor becomes redundant because it is just 'the target has not been hit'; or (b) CONNORS-PURE -- the RSI2 cross IS the exit, targets come out of the ledger entirely, the magnitude floor is DROPPED, and the book accepts many ~breakeven round trips for a high hit rate (note this costs two spreads per trip and would have banked $0.64 net on ROST at 15:01Z). WHAT SHOULD NOT CONTINUE IS RUNNING BOTH, which is what twelve consecutive declines actually are. _CALIBRATION_ENGINE_AND_THE_IN_REGIME_BU.what_it_measures: The margin over the BREAKEVEN win rate implied by the payoff ratio -- never a raw win rate against a fixed number. At payoff 1.0 you need 50%; at payoff 2.0 only 33%. Comparing a win rate to a fixed threshold is the standard way to misread a strategy's health.
_CALIBRATION_ENGINE_AND_THE_IN_REGIME_BU.it_is_not_a_forecaster: It does not classify the regime or predict anything. The primary signal is the strategy's OWN trailing edge -- a direct measurement of whether the edge is present, not a proxy for it. The RSI(2) book is a mean-reversion engine that works in range-bound tapes and degrades in trending ones; measuring the edge catches that without needing to name the regime.
_CALIBRATION_ENGINE_AND_THE_IN_REGIME_BU.THE_BUG_IT_CAUGHT_ON_ITS_FIRST_RUN: Fed the live book's 53 closes, the calibration returned HEALTHY (+22.3 pts) and proposed loosening swing_time_stop_days 14 -> 16. EVERY ONE OF THOSE 53 TRADES CLOSED BEFORE THE TIME STOP EXISTED -- it was dead code until this same commit. The sample contained exactly ZERO evidence about the parameter it wanted to change. Fixed by adding the in_regime_trades argument: a parameter may only be tuned on trades that closed UNDER IT, and after any parameter change that parameter's evidence resets to zero.

If the book is losing money, 'these trades predate the current settings' is not a reason to keep sizing into it. RISK-OFF NEVER WAITS FOR A CLEAN SAMPLE.
_CALIBRATION_ENGINE_AND_THE_IN_REGIME_BU.asymmetry_on_purpose: A degraded edge tightens the entry trigger; a healthy edge does NOT loosen it, and may only earn a slightly longer time stop. A working strategy is not an invitation to take worse setups.

_TIME_STOP_NEEDS_NO_REPORT_BUT_THE_RSI2_.half_one_the_time_stop_reads_no_market_d: Verified by reading the branch (report.py:291-308): it reads ONLY pos['sleeve'], pos['entry_date'] and today's date. It never touches price, rsi2 or ma200 -- the pnl in its message string is cosmetic. So the trigger is pure calendar arithmetic over the LEDGER, and the ledger is reconciled against the broker every run. A stale report cannot make it stale, cannot make it wrong, and cannot certify it either way. The stale-report bar exists to stop the desk acting on decayed TECHNICALS; the time stop has none. It is also the book's ONLY mechanical loss discipline (HARD RULE 5 forbids price stops) and prompt v10 states mechanical exits are NEVER throttled, with FOUR LAWS #2 adding that a cap never delays or blocks an exit. Blocking it is not the 'stricter' branch of the governance tie-breaker -- it is the removal of the only floor the equity book has.
_TIME_STOP_NEEDS_NO_REPORT_BUT_THE_RSI2_.half_two_the_rsi2_exit_does_depend_on_a_: The RSI2>=70 branch reads s['rsi2'], which a day-old report cannot certify. The obvious fix -- compute RSI2 live via get_equity_technical_indicators(type='rsi', period=2, interval='day') -- WORKS, but the two implementations are NOT the same number. Measured against the SAME 2026-09-02 close: MMM report 1.1 vs live 0.8236 (gap 0.28); GD report 1.9 vs live 1.9442 (gap 0.04); ROST report 83.2 vs live 73.1276 (gap 10.07).
_TIME_STOP_NEEDS_NO_REPORT_BUT_THE_RSI2_.the_asymmetry_and_why_it_is_mechanical: The agreement is excellent at the oversold extreme and poor at the overbought one. RSI is bounded [0,100] and a 2-period RSI pinned by two hard down closes collapses to ~0 under ANY smoothing convention, so competing implementations (Wilder vs simple averaging of gains/losses) cannot disagree there. They diverge where up and down closes mix -- the mid and upper range. CONSEQUENCE, and it inverts the intuition: the ENTRY screen (RSI2 < 10) sits in the region where the sources agree to a fraction of a point, and the EXIT trigger (RSI2 >= 70) sits in the region where they differ by ~10 points. A live RSI2 is a safe substitute for the screen and an UNSAFE one for the exit -- backwards from the assumption that an exit is the simpler call.
_TIME_STOP_NEEDS_NO_REPORT_BUT_THE_RSI2_.what_it_licenses_and_what_it_does_not: LICENSED: the first market-hours run may execute PNC's TIME STOP without waiting for the 14:15Z report -- re-quote >=5 min past 13:30Z per the opening-auction rule, confirm placed_agent 'agentic' against the broker, sell, notify Ryan ONCE with evidence. NOT LICENSED: treating a live RSI2 as interchangeable with the report's near the 70 line. Where a live reading lands within ~10 points of 70 and the report disagrees or is silent, WAIT for the fresh report rather than banking or declining off the substitute.
_TIME_STOP_NEEDS_NO_REPORT_BUT_THE_RSI2_.does_it_change_todays_decision: NO, and that is what makes it citable. ROST reads 73.13 live and 83.2 on the report -- both clear 70, so its take-profit fires on either source and the 10-point gap is not load-bearing today. PNC's time stop needs no RSI2 whatsoever. The finding is recorded on a run where it licenses nothing, which is the only condition under which a measurement of the desk's own inputs is credible.

Do NOT carry forward '~10 points' as the typical overbought gap -- that is a single measurement. What IS established: the two sources are demonstrably not interchangeable at the threshold that decides an exit, while being interchangeable at the one that decides an entry. Re-measure before leaning on either.

_OPENING_AUCTION_RULE_APPLIES_TO_EXITS_T.the_mechanism_which_is_the_transferable_: The rule was written in the record as an ENTRY-side price-protection rule (opening auction prints are wide and non-informative). It is symmetric: an exit priced off the same wide auction leg sells low or buys high just as an entry does. The rule's stated purpose in _current_state and CLAUDE.md is 'never PRICE a decision off the opening auction print' -- 'price a decision' covers both sides. A run that reads the rule as entry-only will fire an exit inside the window and collect the artifact.
_OPENING_AUCTION_RULE_APPLIES_TO_EXITS_T.does_it_change_the_decision_to_have_sold: NO. Both exits fire mechanically the moment the market opens: the time stop is calendar-only (15d >= 14d) and the RSI2>=70 print is on yesterday's completed close -- neither is a function of the intraday tape. The rule is about WHEN to price, not WHETHER to trade. Fill quality is the whole cost measured here.
_OPENING_AUCTION_RULE_APPLIES_TO_EXITS_T.the_correction_for_the_next_run: Any run that executes ANY mechanical order (entry OR exit) inside the first 5 minutes past 13:30Z should re-quote and re-check between minutes 5 and 10 unless the position or the sizing would materially decay in that window. For a mechanical exit off yesterday's close there is no such decay -- the rule binds. NOT LICENSED: waiting past the opening window to hunt for a better price -- that is timing the exit, which HARD RULE 5 forbids in reverse. Wait to price honestly, then execute; never wait to price favourably.
_OPENING_AUCTION_RULE_APPLIES_TO_EXITS_T.why_it_survived_previously: The rule was written into every position's _current_state as 'the executing run must re-quote at least ~5 min after 13:30Z per the opening-auction rule' -- clear enough. The failure mode was two runs racing: the 13:33Z run saw the trigger, fetched a live quote (>0Z past bell), and fired. From its own vantage it was following the letter of a rule ('a live quote was taken'); it missed the '>=5 min' clause. Second occurrence of this file's most-repeated defect this session, arriving on an execution instead of a filter -- a check that passes for the wrong reason.
_OPENING_AUCTION_RULE_APPLIES_TO_EXITS_T.honest_scope: n=2, both fills in one collision. The magnitudes are small (-$3.76 = 0.09% of total account value) and one leg (ROST) barely mattered. The finding is that the RULE binds symmetrically, not that the sibling was reckless -- both runs correctly waited on the auction, and one just waited less.

_NO_DENOMINATOR_EXISTS_IN_THE_FIRST_THIR.status: DURABLE. The SYMMETRIC SIBLING of _CLOSING_WINDOW_IS_FORTY_MINUTES_NOT_TWENTY, and a FIFTH denominator mode that is different in KIND from the other four. Read with _PARTICIPATION_IS_A_VETO_NOT_A_GREEN_LIGHT and the 2026-08-26 arc capstone.
_NO_DENOMINATOR_EXISTS_IN_THE_FIRST_THIR.claim: The four known denominator defects are all MIS-CALIBRATIONS -- a baseline that is too strict (session-average inflated by the opening hour, 08-25; trailing window inflated by an event flush, 08-28), too easy (trailing-local drained in a decaying tape, 08-26; closing-auction flow in absolute terms, 08-27/08-28). This one is an ABSENCE. In roughly the first 20-30 minutes of a session there is NO ADMISSIBLE DENOMINATOR AT ALL, because every baseline the clause could use is either the opening auction itself -- which this file's own rules forbid as a denominator -- or the candidate bars being tested, which is circular. A clause with no denominator is not strict or lenient; it is UNEVALUABLE, and an unevaluable confirmation clause means the break is UNCONFIRMED, which means no trade.

_THE_SWING_BOOK_IS_ONE_LOW_BETA_BET_EXPR.the_mechanism_and_it_is_the_transferable: Connors RSI2 selects the most oversold names in a universe. In a persistent melt-up the oversold set IS the funding source for the rally -- the money buying the index is coming OUT of exactly these names. So the screen assembles a short-the-rotation book without ever DECIDING to take that bet, and it does so one name at a time, each of which passes its own gate cleanly. This is the book-level form of _THE_RSI2_SCREEN_IS_BLIND_TO_THE_BOOK: that key found the screen cannot see what is already held; this one finds that even a perfectly diversified-by-sector set of its picks is a single factor exposure.
_THE_SWING_BOOK_IS_ONE_LOW_BETA_BET_EXPR.what_it_does_NOT_license_and_this_is_loa: IT IS NOT A SELL SIGNAL AND MUST NEVER BE READ AS ONE. HARD RULE 5 permits an equity sale on exactly three things -- the RSI2>=70 cross while green, the 14-day time stop, and a HARD RULE 7 thesis break. Relative underperformance is none of them, and the whole point of the no-price-stop policy is that an underwater swing with an intact thesis is HELD. The 14-day time stop is already the mechanism that recycles these if they stall (LLY 09-10, MDLZ 09-11, MMM 09-14, GD 09-15). A run that reads this key as authority to liquidate has inverted it.
_THE_SWING_BOOK_IS_ONE_LOW_BETA_BET_EXPR.what_it_DOES_bear_on: The ENTRY side, and it tightens rather than loosens: adding a FIFTH name off the same oversold screen adds correlated exposure the per-name cap cannot see. Today's three candidates all show the same signature on the same tape -- AMAT -0.77%, LRCX +0.11%, RTX +0.29% against SPY +1.15% / QQQ +1.35%. THE_SECOND_FINDING_a_news_articles_perce.why_it_is_a_new_sub_class: This file already forbids inheriting a mid-event DIRECTIONAL READ (2026-08-28, the Warsh keynote, where every leg of a cross-asset tell flipped in ten minutes) and already has a four-instance family of 'a modelled estimate is never a substitute for a quote' (spot price, ATM strike, wrong expiry board, modelled premium). This is neither. The number was not modelled and not stale-by-inheritance from another run -- it was PUBLISHED, by a human, with attribution and a timestamp, which is exactly what makes it read as authoritative rather than as provisional.
THE_SECOND_FINDING_a_news_articles_perce.the_detector: Re-quote every percentage taken from an article before it enters a grade. The article's own published_at is the tell: a market-wrap percentage is a snapshot of the moment it was written, and an intraday session routinely moves several points past it. Cite the article for the WHY (what management guided, what the analyst said) and the broker for the WHAT (where the stock actually is). Those are different questions and the article is only authoritative on the first.

_THIS_WEEKS_ENTRIES_PREDATE_THE_SIZING_P.WHY_IT_MATTERS_the_in_regime_gate_bites_: The calibration duty may only tune a parameter on trades that closed UNDER IT, and after any parameter change that parameter's evidence RESETS TO ZERO. A calibration run that reaches for the live book's 53-close history to tune the new sizing or time-stop numbers is committing the exact bug calibrate.py caught on its own first run -- tuning a parameter on data that predates it, which is superstition and is indistinguishable from real calibration unless you count.
_THIS_WEEKS_ENTRIES_PREDATE_THE_SIZING_P.THE_ONE_BRANCH_THAT_MAY_STILL_FIRE: The KILL branch is EXEMPT from the in-regime gate by design -- risk-off never waits for a clean sample. _A_VERIFIED_MACRO_FIGURE_WAS_WRONG_BY_AN.headline: The August Employment Situation printed at 12:30Z today: NONFARM PAYROLLS +162,000 vs a Dow Jones consensus of +53,000, UNEMPLOYMENT 4.1% STEADY, July revised UP to +21,000, strongest monthly gain since March. The 2026-09-03T17:50Z key _NFP_IS_INSIDE_EVERY_TACTICAL_WINDOW_OPENED_TODAY recorded the expectation as 'consensus ~475k vs 235k prior, u-rate 5.1% vs 5.2%' -- WRONG BY ROUGHLY AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE ON PAYROLLS AND A FULL POINT ON THE UNEMPLOYMENT RATE. A run inheriting those numbers reads 162k against a remembered 475k as a CATASTROPHIC MISS; against the real 53k it is a 3x BEAT. THE SIGN OF THE SURPRISE INVERTS, which is the single input a post-print regime label is built from.

_A_VERIFIED_MACRO_FIGURE_WAS_WRONG_BY_AN.why_it_survived_and_this_is_the_transfer: THE 09-03 KEY LABELLED ITSELF 'VERIFIED, not assumed' AND CITED THREE SOURCES. That provenance line is exactly what invites the next run to trust it without re-checking -- a confidently-sourced wrong number is more dangerous than an admittedly-uncertain one, which is this file's standing rule that a bullet asserting a hard figure deserves MORE scrutiny, not less. Worse, NOTHING COULD HAVE FLAGGED IT: the 09-03 conclusion (TACTICAL barred into an unresolved print) depended ONLY on the print's TIMING, not on its expected magnitude, so the finding was RIGHT for reasons entirely independent of the numbers it got wrong. A check that passes for the wrong reason -- this file's most-repeated defect -- here arriving as a correct conclusion resting on fabricated inputs.
_A_VERIFIED_MACRO_FIGURE_WAS_WRONG_BY_AN.detector: A macro consensus figure is load-bearing ONLY at the moment the print lands, and that is the moment nobody re-derives it. RE-QUOTE THE CONSENSUS FROM A LIVE SOURCE AT PRINT TIME, never from an inherited watchpoint -- the surprise is actual-minus-consensus and an inherited consensus silently sets the sign. Cheap sanity check that would have caught this one for free: 2026 NFP has been running 20-160k all year, so a '475k consensus' is outside the plausible range of the series and a 5.1% u-rate contradicts the 4.1% that has been printing. AN OUT-OF-RANGE MACRO FIGURE IS A MEASUREMENT BUG UNTIL A PRIMARY SOURCE SAYS OTHERWISE.

_QUOTE_FEED_LAG_MEANS_WALL_CLOCK_CANNOT_.status: DURABLE. Corrects the REMEDY of the 2026-08-21T13:32Z opening-print rule, not its diagnosis.
_QUOTE_FEED_LAG_MEANS_WALL_CLOCK_CANNOT_.headline: THE STANDING FIX -- 'RE-QUOTE AT LEAST ~5 MINUTES AFTER 13:30Z' -- IS CALIBRATED ON WALL-CLOCK TIME, BUT THE ARTIFACT IT GUARDS AGAINST IS A PROPERTY OF THE DATA'S VENUE TIMESTAMP. THE CONNECTOR'S QUOTE FEED LAGS WALL CLOCK BY AN AMOUNT THAT IS NEITHER ZERO NOR CONSTANT, SO WAITING FIVE MINUTES AND RE-QUOTING RETURNED A PRINT FROM INSIDE THE OPENING AUCTION WINDOW -- TWICE.

measurement.fetch_A: wall clock ~13:37:00Z -> SPY venue_last_trade_time 13:31:40.523Z. Lag ~5.4 min.
measurement.fetch_B: wall clock ~13:42:00Z -> SPY venue_last_trade_time 13:33:40.248Z. Lag ~8.3 min.
measurement.the_damning_ratio: Between the two fetches wall clock advanced ~5.0 min while venue time advanced 2.0 min -- the feed progressed at ~40% of real time, i.e. it FELL FURTHER BEHIND. Re-fetching is therefore not guaranteed to walk you out of the opening window; it can walk you deeper into the lag.
measurement.uniform_across_symbols: All 8 symbols in fetch A carried 13:31:34-13:31:40Z venue times (SPY, QQQ, LLY, MDLZ, MMM, GD, NVDA, XLF). A single lagged symbol would be a per-instrument quirk; eight at one timestamp is the feed.
measurement.materiality: Not cosmetic. MMM marked 167.92 in fetch A and 167.5504 in fetch B -- -0.37, -0.22% -- and GD 361.2199 -> 361.295. Position marks and any percentage computed off them move between two reads that a wall-clock rule would call equally settled.

_QUOTE_FEED_LAG_MEANS_WALL_CLOCK_CANNOT_.the_detector: READ venue_last_trade_time ON THE QUOTE, NOT YOUR OWN CLOCK. A print is settled when its VENUE timestamp is at/after ~13:35Z, regardless of when you fetched it. If the venue timestamp is still inside the opening window, the quote is provisional no matter how long you waited -- re-fetch and CHECK AGAIN rather than assuming the wait did it. The same applies to get_option_quotes, which returns quote.updated_at (the SPY 700P hedge read updated_at 13:31:41.8Z in fetch A).
_QUOTE_FEED_LAG_MEANS_WALL_CLOCK_CANNOT_.why_it_survived: This file's most-repeated shape: a check that passes for the wrong reason. A run that waits past 13:35Z and re-quotes has followed the 2026-08-21 rule to the letter, reports 'settled numbers', and is holding opening-auction prints. Nothing errors. The 2026-08-21 incident itself was diagnosed correctly -- an opening print flipped the SIGN of a P/L reported to Ryan -- and the remedy was simply written in the wrong units.
_QUOTE_FEED_LAG_MEANS_WALL_CLOCK_CANNOT_.honest_scope: n=2 fetches on ONE morning, one symbol set. This may be opening-window congestion that clears later in the session rather than a standing property of the feed, and a caching layer in the connector would produce the same signature. Do NOT generalize it into 'the feed is always ~8 minutes late'. The DETECTOR is the durable half and costs nothing: the venue timestamp is returned on every quote already. A later run should re-measure the lag mid-session and record whether it decays.
_QUOTE_FEED_LAG_MEANS_WALL_CLOCK_CANNOT_.changed_no_decision: Correct by the file's own standard for an input audit. No trade was placeable in either book this run -- the equity report on master is stale so signal-sourced trades are barred, and no options trigger existed 7 minutes into the session. Both fetches agree that all four swings are underwater, so the RSI2>=70 take-profit was unavailable on either read.

_THE_CONFIRMATION_CLAUSE_IS_UNREADABLE_A.headline: THE DENOMINATOR ARC HAS A FOURTH WINDOW AND IT IS THE MIRROR OF THE CLOSING ONE: FOR ROUGHLY THE FIRST HALF HOUR, BOTH KNOWN BASELINE DEFECTS ARE LIVE AT THE SAME TIME, SO A VOLUME-CONFIRMATION RATIO COMPUTED AT THE OPEN CARRIES NO INFORMATION IN EITHER DIRECTION.
_THE_CONFIRMATION_CLAUSE_IS_UNREADABLE_A.the_measurement: QQQ 1-minute volume, 2026-09-04 13:30-13:36Z: 208,349 / 104,828 / 80,496 / 53,068 / 38,854 / 77,491 / 35,781. The first bar is 5.8x the seventh, and the decay is monotonic apart from one 13:35 uptick.
_THE_CONFIRMATION_CLAUSE_IS_UNREADABLE_A.why_both_defects_are_live_simultaneously: The 2026-08-25 finding says a SESSION-AVERAGE denominator is too STRICT because the opening hour inflates it. The 2026-08-26 finding says a TRAILING-LOCAL denominator is too EASY in a decaying tape because it tracks participation downward. At the open, the session average does not meaningfully exist yet (it IS the opening bars, so a candidate bar is measured against the auction it is decaying away from), AND the trailing-local mean is collapsing at ~5.8x per six minutes -- the fastest decay any window in this file exhibits. There is no third window to fall back on: the pre-event baseline the 2026-08-28 post-flush correction prescribes requires a quiet stretch of THIS session, and at 13:36Z none has occurred yet.
_THE_CONFIRMATION_CLAUSE_IS_UNREADABLE_A.the_symmetry_that_makes_it_a_rule_rather: The 2026-08-27T19:45Z finding established that the clause is structurally unreadable in the last ~20 minutes because closing-auction flow inflates every bar for reasons unrelated to information. This is the same fact at the other end of the session, driven by the same mechanism (auction flow), and it points the same way: DO NOT let a confirmation ratio decide a TACTICAL entry inside roughly the first 30 minutes. Wait for a stretch of ordinary two-sided trade to exist before asking whether participation 'arrived'.
_THE_CONFIRMATION_CLAUSE_IS_UNREADABLE_A.what_it_does_NOT_say: It does NOT bar trading in the opening window, and it must not be read as widening or narrowing any threshold. It says one specific input -- the volume RATIO -- is uninformative there, so a trigger must stand on its PRICE and STRUCTURE clauses alone in that window, which in practice means it should wait. It is also NOT the same claim as the 2026-09-01 opening-window SLIPPAGE finding (that one is about fill quality on equity entries; this one is about whether an options trigger can be confirmed at all).
_THE_CONFIRMATION_CLAUSE_IS_UNREADABLE_A.honest_scope_it_changed_no_decision: The TACTICAL track was declined this run for a reason that never reached the volume clause: NO LEVEL WAS BREAKING. QQQ closed 09-03 four cents from its 20-day SMA (717.67 vs 717.7140), then GAPPED OVER it -- 13:30Z open 719.41, session low 718.525 -- and never traded down to it. SPY sat flat in a 0.99-point range 3.2 points above its own 20-day. So no ratio was load-bearing, which is the only condition under which a filter's inputs can be audited credibly. Recorded per the standing rule that an audit is creditable precisely when it does not license the trade.
_THE_CONFIRMATION_CLAUSE_IS_UNREADABLE_A.detector: Before letting any volume ratio confirm a break, ask whether the session yet contains a stretch of ORDINARY participation to serve as the denominator. If every available baseline is either the auction itself or a window still decaying away from it, report the ABSOLUTE volume and state that the ratio is unreadable -- do not pick whichever denominator is available and treat its answer as a verdict.

_FEED_LAG_IS_PER_SESSION_NOT_FEED_WIDE.status: DURABLE QUALIFIER on _QUOTE_FEED_LAG_MEANS_WALL_CLOCK_CANNOT_CLEAR_THE_OPENING_WINDOW (13:42Z, same session-day). It STRENGTHENS that finding's detector and CORRECTS its implied model. Read the two together; neither is complete alone.
_FEED_LAG_IS_PER_SESSION_NOT_FEED_WIDE.headline: TWO CONCURRENT RUNS QUOTED THE SAME EIGHT SYMBOLS ~50 SECONDS APART AND GOT VENUE TIMESTAMPS 4.5 MINUTES APART -- WITH THE *EARLIER* FETCH RETURNING THE *FRESHER* DATA. A FEED-WIDE LAG CANNOT DO THAT. THE STALENESS IS A PROPERTY OF THE CONNECTION SERVING YOU, NOT OF THE FEED AT A GIVEN MOMENT.

the_measurement.run_13_42Z_fetch_A: wall ~13:37:00Z -> all eight symbols at venue 13:31:34-13:31:40Z. LAG ~5.4 MINUTES.
the_measurement.the_contradiction: The 13:36:10Z fetch is ~50 seconds EARLIER in wall clock than the 13:37:00Z fetch, yet its data is ~4.5 minutes NEWER. Under a feed-wide lag model, venue time is a monotonic function of wall clock shared by all consumers, so a later fetch can never be staler. It was.
the_measurement.both_were_internally_consistent: Each run saw ALL EIGHT of its symbols carrying one coherent timestamp cluster -- which is exactly why the 13:42Z run correctly ruled out a per-instrument quirk and concluded 'eight at one timestamp is the feed'. That inference is sound about the SCOPE (connection-wide, not per-symbol) and wrong only about the LEVEL (connection, not global).

_FEED_LAG_IS_PER_SESSION_NOT_FEED_WIDE.why_this_matters_more_than_it_looks: The 13:42Z finding's remedy is 'a print is settled when its VENUE timestamp is at/after ~13:35Z, regardless of when you fetched it.' That remedy is CORRECT AND SURVIVES INTACT. What does not survive is any inference from one run's lag to another's -- a run must never conclude 'the feed was lagging at 13:37Z today, so my 13:36Z read was also stale', nor the reverse. Staleness is not a shared property of the clock; it is a property of YOUR quote, and only your own venue timestamp can establish it.
_FEED_LAG_IS_PER_SESSION_NOT_FEED_WIDE.consequence_for_marking_the_book: Three marks for MMM exist within six minutes of one session's open -- 168.00 (venue 13:36:09Z), 167.92 and 167.5504 (venue ~13:31:40Z and ~13:33:40Z). They differ by up to 0.45 (-0.27%). When two runs' marks disagree, DO NOT average them and do NOT prefer the later fetch: prefer the quote with the LATER VENUE TIMESTAMP, which may well be the earlier call.
_FEED_LAG_IS_PER_SESSION_NOT_FEED_WIDE.honest_scope: n=1 collision, two sessions. It CHANGED NO DECISION -- neither run traded (broker re-read at 13:45Z, both order endpoints empty), and both declined both books on grounds that never touched a quote's freshness. That is the only condition under which a data-integrity audit is creditable. The mechanism is NOT established: two sessions hitting different upstream replicas, a per-session cache warming at different rates, and connection-level throttling all fit the observation equally, and this run did not distinguish them. What IS established is the negative claim, which is the useful half: the lag is not a single global quantity, so it cannot be inherited between runs.
_FEED_LAG_IS_PER_SESSION_NOT_FEED_WIDE.detector: Read venue_last_trade_time ON YOUR OWN QUOTE, every time, and treat any print whose venue timestamp sits inside the opening window as provisional no matter how long you waited or what a sibling run observed. If a concurrent run's marks disagree with yours, compare VENUE timestamps rather than fetch times before deciding whose number is real.
_FEED_LAG_IS_PER_SESSION_NOT_FEED_WIDE.family: Fifth member of this file's 'a check that passes for the wrong reason' set applied to measurement infrastructure, after the 5-minute-bucket holes, the 1-minute revisions, the cross-symbol hole signature, and the direction rule. Same shape as the 2026-08-26 correction to the 1-minute arbiter: a rule written to stop trusting a convenient number replaced it with a different convenient number -- here, another run's freshness observation -- and treated that one as authoritative.

_QUOTE_FEED_LAG_READ_THIS_QUALIFIER_FIRS: _FEED_LAG_IS_PER_SESSION_NOT_FEED_WIDE corrects the implied model of _QUOTE_FEED_LAG_MEANS_WALL_CLOCK_CANNOT_CLEAR_THE_OPENING_WINDOW. The detector in that key stands; the phrase 'the feed' in it should be read as 'this connection'.

_THE_ERN_FLAG_IS_FORWARD_ONLY_AND_THE_RS.status: DURABLE, NEW. A structural gap in the [ERN] rule, found by the first run to grade the 2026-09-04T14:02Z report. It CHANGED THIS RUN'S DECISION -- so it is not an audit taken on a quiet day, and the honest-scope note at the bottom applies.
_THE_ERN_FLAG_IS_FORWARD_ONLY_AND_THE_RS.headline: THE [ERN <date>] BAR IS PURELY FORWARD-LOOKING -- IT ASKS WHETHER A PRINT FALLS INSIDE THE HOLD WINDOW AND IS SILENT ON A NAME THAT PRINTED LAST NIGHT. A STOCK THAT JUST GAPPED HARD ON EARNINGS IS THE SINGLE MOST LIKELY NAME TO TOP AN RSI2 OVERSOLD SCREEN THE NEXT MORNING, SO THE FLAG'S BLIND SPOT IS EXACTLY THE POPULATION THE SCREEN OVER-SELECTS.

Under the trend-maturity gate limb (c), the newest analyst revisions must not contradict the position, and here the freshest one is a downgrade.

_THE_ERN_FLAG_IS_FORWARD_ONLY_AND_THE_RS.the_general_rule_and_it_is_the_transfera: The [ERN] rule's stated mechanism is 'a swing straddles a binary event the entry has no edge on, and policy forbids the stop that could protect the gap.' That mechanism has a SIBLING the rule never named: an entry taken IMMEDIATELY AFTER the same binary event, where the desk has no more edge than it would have had before, and where the oversold reading it is acting on is a mechanical artifact of the event rather than a signal. Same event, same absent edge, opposite side of the print. The flag protects against a gap you would HOLD THROUGH; it does nothing about a gap you would BUY INTO.
_THE_ERN_FLAG_IS_FORWARD_ONLY_AND_THE_RS.why_it_matters_MORE_under_the_new_sizing: The 2026-09-02 concentration policy raised the per-name cap to 30% of account value and made [ERN] an ABSOLUTE bar precisely because 'one overnight gap through a print is a ~4-5% account hit' with no price stop. Buying INTO a fresh negative re-rating at that size carries the same exposure to the same event -- the position simply starts on the far side of it. A rule tightened to an absolute bar on one side of a print should not be advisory-to-absent on the other.
_THE_ERN_FLAG_IS_FORWARD_ONLY_AND_THE_RS.THE_DETECTOR_and_it_costs_one_call: Before entering ANY RSI2 name, run get_earnings_calendar with a NEGATIVE days window (a LOOK-BACK) as well as the forward one. A report entry dated within the last 1-2 sessions with verified:true and a non-null eps.actual means the oversold print is an event artifact -- DECLINE. One call covers the whole screen at once, because the calendar is market-wide rather than per-ticker. The report's Earnings column cannot supply this: it is built from the forward calendar by design and was correctly blank.
_THE_ERN_FLAG_IS_FORWARD_ONLY_AND_THE_RS.the_corollary_that_keeps_it_from_becomin: It is a DEFERRAL, exactly like the forward [ERN] rule. A post-earnings name can become a perfectly good setup once the re-rating settles and the gap stops dominating the oscillator -- typically a few sessions, i.e. once RSI(2)'s two-bar window no longer contains the gap. What it cannot be is a MEAN-REVERSION setup on the day of the gap. Re-grade from scratch on post-event numbers; never carry the pre-event grade forward and never carry the deferral forward as though it were a thesis judgment.
_THE_ERN_FLAG_IS_FORWARD_ONLY_AND_THE_RS.honest_scope: n=1, and this one changed the decision -- which is the condition under which this file's own standard says a finding is LEAST credible. Two things carry it anyway. First, the mechanism is STRUCTURAL rather than statistical: RSI(2) is a two-period oscillator and a large gap saturates it arithmetically, so no sample size is needed to establish that a fresh gap produces a low RSI2 print. Second, the earnings date is VERIFIED from the broker's own calendar (verified:true, eps.actual populated), not inferred from the price move. What is NOT established is how often this occurs -- nobody has measured what share of RSI2 screen names printed within the prior two sessions, and a future run could compute it cheaply from the same look-back call.
_THE_ERN_FLAG_IS_FORWARD_ONLY_AND_THE_RS.what_this_does_NOT_change: Nothing about the forward [ERN] rule, which stands in full as an absolute bar. Nothing about the report, which annotated PATH correctly. This ADDS a look-back leg to an existing check; it loosens no gate.

_THE_RAW_IV_RV_RATIO_HAS_A_SCHEDULED_JUM.what_to_actually_do: Quote the pair (raw + ex-gap) as the IV method already requires, and ADD the rolloff date when the artifact is large. For a contract EXPIRING BEFORE the next print, ex-gap is the honest gauge; for one SPANNING a print, raw is, because the buyer genuinely bears that gap. The rolloff schedule matters for a third case the pair does not cover: a CORE swing held 21-45 days will still be open when the denominator jumps, so a position entered on a 'cheap vol' raw reading can find that reading gone while nothing about the position changed.
_THE_RAW_IV_RV_RATIO_HAS_A_SCHEDULED_JUM.honest_scope: This does not say premium is cheap or rich anywhere -- and IV sanity is a NECESSARY condition that never supplies a thesis. It says the raw ratio contains a scheduled, arithmetic, direction-known move that is computable today, and that treating it as new information is a mistake with a date on it. Trimming the top return is itself a crude estimator that UNDERSTATES fat-tail risk; do not swap one headline number for another.
